findings.what: Player clicked action-panel 'Recycle Rune' -> 'Mind Rune (ready)'. The ready (untapped) Mind Rune was recycled straight to the rune deck (10->11) yielding only Mind power 1; energy stayed 0 -> 0.
findings.why_wrong: DESIGN.md (Interactions): 'Recycling an untapped rune auto-taps it first for +1 energy (you'd always do this), shown as a +1 float.' A basic rune has both '[T]: Add [1]' and 'Recycle this: Add [C]' (rule 157.2); recycling a ready rune without tapping throws away 1 energy for no benefit. The action-panel recycle path bypassed the auto-tap that the design mandates (expected after-state: energy 1, mind 1). No +1 float shown either.
findings.reason: The action-panel sub-button for a "(ready)" recycleRune group (actions.js:378-397, specifically the onclick at line 385/394) calls executeMove("recycleRune", m.params, ...) directly with no preceding exhaustRune. The code even acknowledges at actions.js:339-342 ([rule:ui-recycle-rune-ready-split]) that "recycling the ready one forfeits its energy" and only mitigates by sorting exhausted groups first — it never auto-taps. By contrast the right-click path interactions.js:424-455 (quickRecycleRune) exhausts first then recycles, per .claude/skills/riftbound-rules/DESIGN.md:24 "Recycling an untapped rune auto-taps it first for +1 energy (you'd always do this), shown as a +1 float." Trace step 1->2 matches: Mind Rune ready, energy 0->0. Caveat: DESIGN.md:24 sits under the "Right-click rune = recycle" bullet, so one could argue the mandate is scoped to right-click; but the stated rationale ("you'd always do this" / "strictly better") is path-independent and the action-panel path produces the strictly-worse outcome with no +1 float.

findings.why_wrong: Aspirant's Climb rulesText: "Increase the points needed to win the game by 1." The engine models this as players[*].victoryScoreModifier (+1, effective threshold 9 via win-conditions/victory.ts), but apps/riftbound-app/server/snapshot.ts ships only base state.victoryScore and public/js/gameplay/renderer.js:99 / game-flow.js:181 render `${victoryPoints} / ${gameState.victoryScore}` ignoring the modifier, so the player is told they win at 8 when the game actually requires 9.

"?"`; neither adds player.victoryScoreModifier. The engine does apply the modifier in this game: pregame.ts:302 executes `transitionToPlay`, which calls applyBattlefieldPermanentEffects (setup.ts:407); battlefield-setup-effects.ts:45-52 bumps every player's victoryScoreModifier by 1 for the `increase-victory-score` static on aspirants-climb.ts (registry keyed by instance id `player-2-bf-ogn-276-298`, registered with abilities via pregame.ts:175/182 + cards.ts:121). Win check uses getEffectiveVictoryScore = victoryScore + modifier (victory.ts:18-32), so effective threshold is 9 while badge shows /8 (base 8 from game-modes.ts:67). Minor nit: snapshot.ts:412 does ship `players` (incl. victoryScoreModifier) alongside victoryScore at :417, so the data is available client-side but unused — the display bug stands.

findings.reason: Visual defect is real; the DOM-count evidence is not. (1) board.js:121-127 renders the moved Recruit into `.bf-units.player-side` (last child, bottom of the battlefield body) and card.js:151-153 gives it `card--exhausted`, so the card IS in the DOM. But showdown.js:251 appends `.battlefield__showdown-panel` into the same `.battlefield`, and gameplay.css:927-941 makes that panel `position:absolute; left:8px; right:8px; bottom:8px; z-index:6; background rgba(14,10,26,0.92)` while `.bf-units` sits at z-index:1 (gameplay.css:1090-1102) with no padding/space reserved for the panel. In the fixed 1920x1080 logical layout the battlefield body is ~150px tall, so the opaque panel fully covers the player-side unit row — exactly what 37.png/40.png show: header, empty opponent row, then the PASS FOCUS/CONQUER panel, no Recruit and no sideways/exhausted rendering visible. (2) The 'DOM shows 0 exhausted' invariant is a harness false positive: monkey-drive.ts:93 counts `[id^="bf-"] .card.card--exhausted, .bf-zone .card.card--exhausted`, but the UI uses `.battlefield[data-bf-id] .bf-units` — neither selector exists anywhere in public/, so bfExhausted is always 0. Net: the player's just-moved exhausted unit is hidden behind the showdown panel (gameplay.css:927), confirming the misrepresentation, though the cited invariantViolation itself is spurious.

findings.why_wrong: Per the showdown/control rules, when all relevant players pass with an empty chain the showdown ends and control/conquer is established automatically (516.5.b showdown at empty uncontrolled battlefield -> attacker gains control on close; scoring 629-632). Conquer is not a player-elected action, so presenting it as a button/step is a rules misrepresentation (not exercised this step, hence low).
findings.reason: UI: showdown.js:174-177 computes `conquerMove = readyToClose ? findShowdownMove("conquerBattlefield", battlefieldId) : null` and lines 207-213 unconditionally render a `Conquer` button with hint `Q` in the showdown panel, titled "Conquer (both sides must pass first)" when disabled / "Conquer (Q)" when enabled — presenting conquer as a manual post-pass step. Engine: moves/combat/conquer-battlefield.ts:27-131 defines `conquerBattlefield` as a player-enumerated Discretionary Action (enumerator returns it for the active player in neutral-open when they solely occupy a non-controlled battlefield). Rules 347.2.a/348/348.2.a (rule.ts lookup) say when all players pass the Showdown Closes and the sole remaining player *establishes Control* (→ Conquer per 348.2.a.1) automatically — not a player-elected action. Note the engine's passShowdownFocus reducer (moves/chain/showdown.ts:93-135) does already auto-establish control on non-combat close, so the button is largely vestigial, but both the UI button and the player-exposed conquerBattlefield move exist exactly as claimed. Trace step 37 has interaction.showdown.active=true so the panel (and button) was rendered.

findings.what: After the Recruit token was Standard-Moved from base to Back-Alley Bar (step 37) and through step 38, the engine has it at the battlefield with exhausted=true, but the battlefield renders no unit at all — the in-card SHOWDOWN banner (Pass Focus / Conquer) occupies the unit rows, dom.bfExhausted=0, and the harness flags 'engine has 1 exhausted board cards, DOM shows 0' on steps 37-40. The player cannot see the unit they just moved nor that it is exhausted.
findings.why_wrong: Units at a battlefield are public board state and a moved unit must be shown exhausted (Standard Move exhausts the unit; exhausted permanents are displayed rotated, rule 143.4 / Exhaust game action). Hiding the only unit at the contested battlefield during its own showdown misrepresents the board.
findings.ruleOrCard: 143.4 (exhausted state) / Standard Move; Recruit token at Back-Alley Bar
findings.reason: Screenshots 37-40 show the Back-Alley Bar battlefield with only the header, an empty opponent row, and the SHOWDOWN panel — the just-moved exhausted Recruit token is not visible anywhere. Source: render/board.js:125-127 puts the viewer's units in the last row (.bf-units.player-side, z-index:1 per gameplay.css:1090-1104) at the bottom of .bf-body, and showdown.js:184-198 / board.js:151-158 inject .battlefield__showdown-panel into the same .battlefield element, which gameplay.css:927-933 styles as `position:absolute; left:8px; right:8px; bottom:8px; z-index:6` with an opaque background — it sits directly on top of the player-side unit row, and at this battlefield height (~115px, .battlefield overflow:hidden at css:878) the row is fully occluded for the entire showdown. Caveat: the harness's dom.bfExhausted=0 is itself a selector bug (monkey-drive.ts:93 queries `[id^="bf-"] .card.card--exhausted, .bf-zone .card.card--exhausted`, which matches nothing in this DOM — battlefields use #battlefieldRow/.battlefield/.bf-units), so the card element likely exists in the DOM with card--exhausted; the confirmed defect is the visual occlusion by the showdown panel, not a missing render call.

findings.what: After the (correctly rejected, rule 144.1.c) drag of Otterpus to Back-Alley Bar during the showdown, the board still does not show the Recruit token that is actually AT Back-Alley Bar. Engine state has bfZones[Back-Alley Bar] = [Recruit, exhausted:true], but the battlefield panel's unit row is completely covered by the 'SHOWDOWN in progress' banner, dom.bfExhausted=0, and the harness invariant 'exhausted-rendered' fires (engine 1 exhausted board card, DOM 0). The player cannot see the unit that is contesting the battlefield nor that it is exhausted.
findings.why_wrong: A unit that performed a Standard Move is exhausted as its cost (144.2) and is now located at the battlefield (rule 143.4 / 420); the UI must render board units in their zone with exhausted orientation. Hiding the contesting unit behind the showdown overlay misrepresents the game state during the exact window (showdown, 548) where the player must decide whether to pass focus or react.
findings.reason: The inline showdown panel is injected as a child of the `.battlefield` element (render/board.js:151-158 -> showdown.js:185 `panel.className = "battlefield__showdown-panel"`) and styled at gameplay.css:927-941 as `position:absolute; left:8px; right:8px; bottom:8px; z-index:6; background: rgba(14,10,26,0.92)`. The player's unit row `.bf-units.player-side` is the last flex child at the bottom of `.bf-body` with only `z-index:1` (gameplay.css:1090-1117), inside `.battlefield {overflow:hidden}` (866-879). So the opaque panel sits directly on top of the player-side unit row. Screenshot 39.png (cropped) confirms: Back-Alley Bar shows header + empty opponent row + the SHOWDOWN panel; the Recruit card is only a faint sliver peeking out from under the CONQUER button, not legible and its exhausted state not visible. Engine state has the Recruit (owner player-1, exhausted:true) in battlefield-player-1-bf-ogn-277-298 for steps 37-39. Caveat: the harness figure dom.bfExhausted=0 is itself unreliable — monkey-drive.ts:93 queries `[id^="bf-"] .card.card--exhausted, .bf-zone .card.card--exhausted`, neither of which exists in the real DOM (`#battlefieldRow .battlefield .bf-units .card`), so that invariant would fire regardless. But the substantive UI defect (showdown overlay hides the contesting unit and its exhausted state) is real per CSS + screenshot.

findings.what: The base-zone card (Otterpus) is rendered floating over the bottom of the Aspirant's Climb battlefield panel and on top of the Resources bar, partially covering the 'Runes 4/4' readout (same in 38.png and 39.png).
findings.why_wrong: Base and Battlefield are distinct board zones (rules 106-108 zone model); drawing a base unit overlapping a battlefield panel makes it ambiguous which location the unit is at, and it occludes the resource bar the player needs to read energy/runes.
findings.reason: 38.png shows Otterpus (100x140 logical card) and the player legend/champion both vertically centered on y~437, spilling up over the Aspirant's Climb panel / battlefield-row bottom border (~y430) and down over the resource bar (~y445-473). Source explains it deterministically: the player base row wrapper is `<div style="display:flex; gap:6px; align-items:center; min-height:0;">` (gameplay.html:159) inside `.player-area { min-height: 0 }` (gameplay.css:133-141). Every other player-area child is flex-shrink:0 (.resource-bar css:2513-2522, hand cards css:252-255, legend-champion-zone css:537-543), so when board content exceeds the fixed 1080px canvas the base row wrapper is the only thing that shrinks — it collapses toward 0 height while its children (#player-base min-height:100px css:229-234 holding a 140px .card css:277-280, and the 120px legend/champion cards) keep their size and, because of align-items:center, overflow equally above (onto the battlefield row, painted later in DOM so on top) and below. `#player-base { position: relative }` (css:3437-3439) additionally lifts it in paint order above the non-positioned .resource-bar sibling, so the card occludes the Runes readout. Not a drag ghost: identical in step 38 (click-action) and 39.

findings.what: After clicking 'Recycle Rune (4 available)' (which only expanded the Mind/Order submenu — no state change, which is fine), the board still fails to render the exhausted Recruit token that is at Back-Alley Bar (bfZones shows Recruit exhausted=true; dom.bfExhausted=0, invariant 'engine has 1 exhausted board cards, DOM shows 0'). In 40.png the Back-Alley Bar unit row is entirely covered by the 'SHOWDOWN in progress' banner, so the attacking unit is not visible at all, let alone rotated.
findings.why_wrong: Rule 143.4 / exhausted state must be visibly represented; the unit that moved to the battlefield and triggered this non-combat showdown (516.5.b / 548) is the only unit there and the player cannot see it or its exhausted status while being asked to Pass Focus / act in the showdown.
findings.ruleOrCard: 143.4 (exhausted representation); Recruit token at Back-Alley Bar
findings.reason: Two parts. (1) The invariant evidence (dom.bfExhausted=0) is a HARNESS false positive, not a UI bug: monkey-drive.ts:93 counts `[id^="bf-"] .card.card--exhausted, .bf-zone .card.card--exhausted`, but the app renders battlefield units under `#battlefieldRow .battlefield .bf-units` (render/board.js:107-127) and no element with id^="bf-" or class .bf-zone exists anywhere in public/ — so bfExhausted is always 0. The token IS emitted into the DOM with the exhausted class (render/card.js:151-153; owner set via create-token.ts:108 so board.js:92 keeps it in playerUnits). (2) The user-visible defect described — the sole attacking unit at Back-Alley Bar is invisible during the showdown — is real and by construction: gameplay.css:927-942 `.battlefield__showdown-panel { position:absolute; left:8px; right:8px; bottom:8px; z-index:6; background: rgba(14,10,26,0.92) }` is appended into the .battlefield (showdown.js:252) with no space reserved (.showdown-active-bf at css:900 only changes border/shadow), so the ~75px opaque panel sits directly over `.bf-units.player-side` (z-index:1, bottom of .bf-body). 38.png/40.png show the panel fully covering the player-side row; the exhausted Recruit cannot be seen while the player is asked to Pass Focus/Conquer.

findings.what: Activated ability cost 'Recycle 1 from your trash' is never paid or required
findings.expected: Ability should be unavailable with an empty trash; when activated it should prompt for / recycle 1 card from trash to the deck as the cost before giving +1 Might
findings.observed: With trash=0, activateAbility was listed and resolved (+1 mightModifier). With 1 card in trash (Stacked Deck), activating left trash at 1 and deck at 33 (nothing recycled, no pendingChoice), still gave +1 Might; could be repeated indefinitely for free (mightModifier reached 2). Parsed ability has cost {recycle:1} but engine ignores it.
findings.reason: activate-ability.ts handles only energy/power/xp/exhaust/discard/kill costs; `recycle` is never checked or paid. Condition block (activate-ability.ts:401-503) has no trash-size gate for cost.recycle, and the reducer's pay-cost block (activate-ability.ts:854-903, plus deductAbilityCost at :251-291) never moves a trash card to deck or raises a pendingChoice. `grep -i recycle activate-ability.ts` returns nothing. Parser does emit `{recycle: N}` costs (riftbound-cards parser/__tests__/effects/recycle.test.ts:155-182), so Vi's ability activates for free with empty trash and repeats indefinitely.

findings.what: Target restriction 'enemy Calm unit' ignores the Calm domain requirement
findings.expected: Only enemy units of the Calm domain should be legal targets
findings.observed: playSpell moves offered enemy Eager Drakehound (domain fury) as a target alongside the two enemy Calm units; playing it on Drakehound resolved and dealt 4 (killed it, sent to trash). Parsed target is {type:unit, controller:enemy} with no domain filter.
findings.reason: ven-015-166 has abilities:[null] in ven.json so it is parsed at runtime via effects-damage.ts:91-94 ("Deal N to TARGET") -> parseCardTarget. parseCardTarget (riftbound-cards/src/parser/impl/targets.ts:11-85) only extracts controller (line 27-31), quantity, location, and damaged/stunned/mighty filters (76-82); it never inspects domain words like "Calm", so "an enemy Calm unit" yields {type:"unit", controller:"enemy"}. Verified by running getCardRegistry().get("ven-015-166"): effect = {type:"damage", amount:4, target:{type:"unit", controller:"enemy"}} with no domain restriction.

findings.what: 'This can't be countered' not implemented
findings.expected: A counter effect (Wind Wall) targeting Decree of Rage should fail / Decree should still resolve and deal 4
findings.observed: Played Wind Wall while Decree was on the chain; Decree chain item became countered:true, resolved with no effect (Whiteflame Protector damage stayed 0), Decree went to trash. Parsed ability carries no uncounterable flag.
findings.reason: No uncounterable support exists anywhere. Card def riftbound-cards/src/data/sets/ven.json:727 (ven-015-166) has abilities: [null] — "This can't be countered." is not parsed (no 'countered' handling in riftbound-cards/src/**/*.ts). Engine counter paths unconditionally mark the target: abilities/effects/counter.ts:16-18 (handle_counter sets targetItem.countered = true with only a !countered check) and game-definition/moves/chain/counter.ts:37-44,56-57 (counterSpell condition/reducer check only existence and !countered). resolve.ts:37 then skips countered items. No 'uncounterable'/'cantBeCountered' identifier exists in riftbound-engine/src. So Wind Wall countering Decree of Rage succeeds, matching the observed behavior.

findings.what: Countered spell is not returned to owner's hand
findings.expected: Per rulesText 'Counter a spell. Return it to its owner's hand instead of putting it in their trash.' -- after Abandon counters Cleave, Cleave should go to player-1's hand.
findings.observed: Cleave was marked countered:true on the chain, then on resolution went to trash (trash = [Abandon, Cleave]; hand did not contain Cleave). The parsed Abandon effect is just {type:'counter'} with no return-to-hand replacement.
findings.reason: Parser output for Abandon's rulesText is sequence[{type:'counter'},{type:'predict'}] — the "Return it to its owner's hand instead" clause is dropped (riftbound-cards/src/parser/parsers/effect-parser.ts:275-287 emits bare {type:'counter'}). Engine: abilities/effects/counter.ts:5-19 only sets targetItem.countered=true, no destination override. On resolution, game-definition/moves/chain/resolve.ts:37 skips countered effect, then settleResolvedSpellCard (resolve.ts:259-272) moves the card to resolved.resolveTo ?? 'trash'; ChainItem.resolveTo (chain/chain-state.ts:67) only allows 'trash'|'banishment' — no hand option. So countered Cleave goes to trash, not owner's hand.

findings.what: Predict gives no look / no optional-recycle choice; silently auto-recycles the top card
findings.expected: '[Predict] (Look at the top card of your Main Deck. You may recycle it.)' -- player should be shown the top card and get a may-recycle prompt (pendingChoice), with the option to leave it on top.
findings.observed: No pendingChoice or UI prompt at any point; no log line. Deck top card player-1-main-22-ogn-016-298 was moved to the bottom automatically (top before=main-22, after: top=main-23, bottom=main-22). handle_predict in abilities/effects/predict.ts unconditionally recycles top N.
findings.reason: predict.ts:6-31: handle_predict takes top N of mainDeck and unconditionally moveCard(position:"bottom") for each (lines 23-30), with no pendingChoice, no reveal/look, and no log. The comment at lines 8-15 explicitly admits it auto-recycles for headless play and that a full impl "would pause for a player Choice ... via pendingChoice". Matches observed main-22 moved to bottom with no prompt.

findings.what: Abandon can be played with no spell on the chain (no valid target for 'Counter a spell')
findings.expected: Rule 355.8: valid choices must be made for all targets to put a spell on the chain; with an empty chain Abandon should not be offered/playable.
findings.observed: With chain empty, pw moves listed playSpell for Abandon (no targets param); executing it charged 2 energy, put Abandon on the chain with no targets, and on resolution it still performed the Predict auto-recycle.
findings.reason: Abandon parses to a spell ability {type:"sequence", effects:[{type:"counter"} (no target descriptor), {type:"predict", amount:1}]}. In play-spell.ts the only target gate is spellEffectHasLegalTargets (play-spell.ts:172-179 condition, :297 enumerator) which, for a sequence, checks each sub-effect via targetDescriptorIsSatisfiable (targeting.ts:196-199, 254-261) — an effect with no `target` returns true, so a target-less `counter` never blocks the play. Reaction timing is always legal (chain/chain-state.ts:178-181), so the enumerator emits playSpell for Abandon with no targets even when interaction.chain is null. No code anywhere checks that a spell exists on the chain for a `counter` effect (grep for "counter" in play/targeting/target-resolver finds nothing). At resolution, handle_counter (abilities/effects/counter.ts:5-20) silently no-ops when the chain has no item beneath it, and the sequence proceeds to the predict step — matching the observed behavior. Rule 355.8 gate is missing for counter-a-spell effects.

findings.what: Showdown-begins trigger does not fire for a non-combat showdown at Diana's battlefield
findings.expected: Moving Diana alone to an empty uncontrolled battlefield opens a (non-combat) showdown there (rules 344/345); 'When a showdown begins here' should put Diana's optional pay-[1] trigger on the chain / prompt
findings.observed: interaction.showdown became active (isCombatShowdown:false, battlefield = Diana's), but chain stayed empty, no pendingChoice, energy unchanged (4). Trigger only fired later when Diana moved into an enemy-occupied battlefield (combat showdown) — card def encodes trigger as {event:'attack', on:{location:'here'}} instead of a showdown-begins event
findings.reason: Card def /root/src/tcg/tcg-engines/packages/riftbound-cards/src/cards/unl/diana-lunari.ts:28-31 encodes the trigger as `{ event: "attack", on: { location: "here" } }`. In the engine, standard-move.ts:298-311 fires "attack" triggers only inside `if (hasOpponentUnit)` (combat showdown); non-combat showdowns opened via startShowdownState fire no event, and abilities/game-events.ts has no showdown-begins event type at all. So "When a showdown begins here" never fires for a non-combat showdown, matching the observation.

findings.what: Predict gives no look/recycle choice
findings.expected: Predict: player looks at top card of Main Deck and MAY recycle it (player choice prompt)
findings.observed: After accepting the opt-in, no predict prompt appeared; engine silently auto-recycled the top card (Blood Rush moved from deck top to bottom). handle_predict in abilities/effects/predict.ts unconditionally recycles top N
findings.reason: handle_predict at packages/riftbound-engine/src/abilities/effects/predict.ts:16-30 unconditionally moves the top N deck cards to the bottom with no pendingChoice; the in-code comment (lines 7-15) explicitly admits it auto-recycles for headless play and that a full implementation would pause for player choice. Diana, Lunari (unl-079-219, cards/unl/diana-lunari.ts:16) emits { type: "predict", amount: 1 }, so the player never gets the look/may-recycle prompt the card text requires.

findings.what: 'Reveal the top card; if it's a spell, draw it' resolves as reveal-until-spell + banish + play-to-board
findings.expected: Reveal exactly one card (the top card). If it is a spell put it into hand; otherwise nothing else happens. Deck order otherwise unchanged, no extra chain items
findings.observed: Engine scanned the deck until the first spell: 10 non-spell cards (Serrated Dirk..Noxus Saboteur) were recycled to the bottom, the spell hit (Hextech Ray) was moved to banishment, a new chain item 'Hextech Ray — ability' with effect {type:'move',to:'choose'} was added, then a choose-destination pendingChoice (base / battlefield-player-1) appeared and picking 'base' placed the Hextech Ray spell card onto the base as a permanent. Hand never gained a card. (card encodes effect as reveal{until:'spell',then:{draw:1}} which routes into the Dazzling-Aurora reveal-until handler in abilities/effects/reveal.ts)
findings.reason: Card def /root/src/tcg/tcg-engines/packages/riftbound-cards/src/cards/unl/diana-lunari.ts:17-23 encodes the effect as {type:'reveal', amount:1, from:'deck', until:'spell', then:{draw:1}}. handle_reveal in /root/src/tcg/tcg-engines/packages/riftbound-engine/src/abilities/effects/reveal.ts:15-55 branches solely on `until` + from==='deck', ignores `amount` and `then`, scans the whole deck for the first card with cardType===until (l.23-30), moves the hit to 'banishment' (l.32-35), adds a chain item with effect {type:'move', to:'choose', target:hit} (l.37-47), and recycles all preceding cards to bottom (l.49-54). No draw-to-hand path exists. Matches the observed reveal-until + banish + move-to-choose behavior.

findings.what: Unit returned to hand by Rebuke keeps its exhausted state
findings.expected: A card moving board->hand becomes a new object (rule 124); hand card should have no exhausted flag and render upright
findings.observed: After Rebuke resolved on exhausted Gust Monk, pw state shows Gust Monk in hand with exhausted:true and the hand renders it rotated sideways (screenshot /tmp/card-ogn-172-298-after.png)
findings.reason: handle_returnToHand (packages/riftbound-engine/src/abilities/effects/return-to-hand.ts:19-24) only calls ctx.zones.moveCard(... "hand") with no meta reset; core moveCard (packages/core/src/operations/operations-impl.ts:174-251) only updates zone/position and never touches cardMetas; state-based-checks has no step clearing board state for hand cards (contrast the kill path at cleanup/state-based-checks.ts:257-266 which explicitly sets exhausted:false). Reproduced with harness: exhausted P2 unit at bf1, P1 casts ogn-172-298 targeting it, settle -> zone=hand, meta {"exhausted":true,"__flags":{"exhausted":true}}, isExhausted=true.

findings.what: Static ability "Enemy units here with less Might than me don't deal combat damage" is not implemented (parser drops the clause).
findings.expected: With Vilemaw (8 Might) at the battlefield, the three enemy Mech tokens (3 Might each, all < 8) should deal no combat damage, so co-attacker Overzealous Fan (2 Might) should survive combat.
findings.observed: After resolveFullCombat, Overzealous Fan was killed and sent to trash (Mechs dealt their 9 combat damage normally). Running the card's rulesText through parseAbilities() yields only [{keyword:Ambush},{triggered hold -> draw 1}] — the second sentence produces no ability at all.
findings.reason: Card def /root/src/tcg/tcg-engines/packages/riftbound-cards/src/cards/unl/vilemaw.ts:4-16 has no `abilities` field, only rulesText (line 13-14). Running parseAbilities() on that rulesText yields exactly [{keyword:Ambush},{triggered hold->draw 1}] — the "Enemy units here with less Might than me don't deal combat damage" sentence produces no ability. The engine has no combat-damage-prevention static effect (grep for noCombatDamage/less Might/unl-060 in riftbound-engine/src finds nothing outside an unrelated comment in abilities/effects/move.ts:62), so combat resolves normally and enemy units deal full damage.

findings.what: Static 'Friendly buffed units have [Deflect]' never applies when the unit was buffed in-game (including by Spirit's Refuge's own play trigger).
findings.expected: After Spirit's Refuge's trigger buffs Chemtech Enforcer, that unit should carry Deflect (meta.grantedKeywords should include {keyword:'Deflect',duration:'static'}) as long as it stays buffed.
findings.observed: Live game: Chemtech Enforcer meta = {buffed:true,...} with no grantedKeywords at all, even after further moves (server /api/game/:id/state confirms). Reproduced in engine harness: play refuge from hand -> pick real unit ogn-175-298 -> isBuffed true, might 4, grantedKeywords [] (still [] after addResources and advanceTurn). The grant only lands when the unit is pre-seeded with meta {buffed:true} in the scenario builder, so the static's filter:'buffed' check does not see buffs applied by the runtime buff effect.
findings.reason: Reproduced in harness: P1 with two friendly units + Spirit's Refuge in hand; play refuge -> pick decision -> pick "enf" -> enf meta {buffed:true,__flags:{buffed:true}}, might 4, grantedKeywords [] — still [] after advanceTurn (turn 2->3). With only one friendly unit (auto-target, no pick) Deflect IS granted, so the static filter itself (static-abilities.ts:408-414 reads meta[filter]===true; buff.ts:23-26 mirrors meta.buffed=true) is fine. Root cause is that recalculateStaticEffects never runs after the picked buff: pending-choice.ts:534-554 (choose-target branch of resolvePendingChoice reducer) calls executeEffect(choice.effect…) and returns with no cleanup/static recalc; withPostMoveCleanup (cleanup/post-move-cleanup.ts:97) is defined but never applied to riftboundMoves (game-definition/moves/index.ts:30, definition.ts:37), and the flow's cleanup phase is a no-op (riftbound-flow.ts:653-667 onBegin only sets phase). Instrumented run confirmed zero recalculateStaticEffects/runStateMaintenance calls after the pick and through endTurn. So the static grant only lands when some other path (chain resolve, counters move, play-self trigger, or scenario pre-seed at build) happens to trigger a recalc.

findings.what: Even when Deflect is granted via the static, opponents are not charged the [rainbow] surcharge to target the unit.
findings.expected: Opponent choosing a friendly buffed (Deflect) unit with a spell must pay 1 power (rule 721); with 0 power the cast targeting that unit should be illegal.
findings.observed: Harness: P1 has Spirit's Refuge + pre-buffed Shipyard Skulker showing grantedKeywords [{Deflect,static}]; P2 with energy 5 and NO power casts Cleave (ogn-004-298) targeting Skulker -> accepted (ok=true). getDeflectSurcharge in moves/play/cost.ts only reads printed keyword abilities / registry.hasKeyword and ignores meta.grantedKeywords.
findings.reason: getDeflectSurcharge (moves/play/cost.ts:366-387) computes the surcharge solely from registry.getAbilities(targetId) printed keyword abilities and registry.hasKeyword(targetId,"Deflect"); CardDefinitionRegistry.hasKeyword (operations/card-lookup.ts:122-133) only inspects the static card definition (def.keywords / def.abilities). Neither path reads card meta grantedKeywords, so Deflect granted by Spirit's Refuge's static yields surcharge 0 and an opponent with 0 power can legally target the buffed unit.

findings.what: Attack trigger does not reveal the top 2 cards of the Main Deck and never offers to banish/play one of them or recycle the rest.
findings.expected: On accepting the optional trigger: reveal top 2 of P1's main deck (Overzealous Fan, Mystic Poro), prompt to optionally banish one and play it (unit may be played 'here'), recycle the other to the bottom.
findings.observed: After accepting the opt-in prompt, P1's deck was untouched (top 3 still Overzealous Fan / Mystic Poro / Dangerous Duo, count 35 before and after), no reveal UI or pick prompt for deck cards, nothing recycled. Harness repro with deckTop top1/top2: both remain in mainDeck after the ability resolves.
findings.reason: reksai-swarm-queen.ts:20 emits `{ amount: 2, from: "deck", type: "reveal" }` with no `until`. abilities/effects/reveal.ts:14-15 gates the entire handler on `revEff.until && from === "deck"`; otherwise handle_reveal does nothing ("Without `until` the reveal is purely informational" — no reveal state, no prompt, no deck movement). The following steps in the sequence (banish target {type:"card"} at line 21, recycle from:"board" at line 28) resolve via target-resolver.ts which collects candidates from the board only (lines 142/255-272), never mainDeck. So top-2 deck cards are never revealed, offered for banish/play, or recycled — matches the observed untouched deck.

findings.what: The 'banish one, then play it' steps target an arbitrary board card — the ENEMY defending unit — instead of one of the revealed cards.
findings.expected: Only one of the two revealed deck cards may be banished/played; enemy units at the battlefield must be unaffected.
findings.observed: Live: the P2 Recruit token defending at Aspirant's Climb was moved to banishment, then a P2-controlled 'Recruit — move to choose' item appeared on the chain and after resolution an ownerless ghost entry 'token-recruit-player-2-42' (cardType unknown, owner '') sits in the base zone; combat showdown continues with no defender. Harness: enemy 'foe' (ogn-175-298) ends in banishment and P2 is prompted 'Choose a destination for Shipyard Skulker' (base | battlefield-bf1). Card def uses banish target {type:'card'} + play target pending-value, which resolves against the board rather than the revealed set.
findings.reason: Card def reksai-swarm-queen.ts:20-30: step 0 `{type:"reveal", amount:2, from:"deck"}` has no `until`, and abilities/effects/reveal.ts:14-15 makes such a reveal a pure no-op (no revealed set is recorded, deck untouched). Step 1 `{type:"banish", target:{type:"card"}}` (line 21, and pendingValue.source=1 at line 30) resolves via getTargetIds -> resolveTarget (target-resolver.ts:87ff): `type:"card"` falls through to getBoardCardIds (base + battlefield units of ALL players, lines 257-281) with no controller/location filter, excludes only self, and slices to the first candidate (line ~250) — i.e. an arbitrary board card such as the enemy defender. banish.ts:28-33 moves it to banishment; sequence.ts:122-124 captures it as `pending`, and step 2 `play target:pending-value toLocation:"here"` then plays that enemy card (owner P2 -> P2-controlled move/choose chain item). Nothing constrains the choice to the two top-of-deck cards, so the observed enemy Recruit banish + P2 destination prompt follows directly from the card definition.

findings.what: 'channel 1 rune exhausted' option of the conquer trigger misplaces the rune and ignores 'exhausted'
findings.expected: Choosing the channel option moves the top rune of player-1's rune deck into the runePool zone, exhausted, usable like other runes (rule 606.2)
findings.observed: Rune deck 8->7, but the channeled rune (player-1-rune-4-ogn-007-298) landed in zone 'base' (not 'runePool'), meta.exhausted=false, and no exhaustRune/recycleRune move is offered for it. Engine handler packages/riftbound-engine/src/abilities/effects/channel.ts hardcodes targetZoneId:'base' and never reads effect.exhausted. UI renders the rune floating over the board center instead of in the rune row.
findings.reason: packages/riftbound-engine/src/abilities/effects/channel.ts:14-17 — handle_channel does ctx.zones.moveCard({cardId, targetZoneId: "base"}) hardcoded, never sets exhausted meta and never reads effect.exhausted. The proper rune zone is "runePool" (game-definition/moves/resources.ts:59,81,105 — channel move targets runePool and exhaustRune requires zone === "runePool"), so a channeled rune in 'base' is unexhausted and unusable by exhaustRune/recycleRune.

findings.what: Sidebar 'CHOOSE A CARD' panel renders the two mode options as 'undefined'
findings.expected: Sidebar lists 'draw 1' / 'channel 1 rune exhausted' like the modal does
findings.observed: Modal correctly shows 'draw 1' / 'channel 1', but the right-hand Available Actions panel shows two buttons both labelled 'undefined' for the choose-mode pendingChoice
findings.reason: actions.js:229-237 (sidebar pending-choice buttons) derives label from pickedCardId ?? pickedZoneId ?? pickedName; choose-mode moves carry only params.pickedMode (pending-choice.ts:299), so cid is undefined, accept isn't boolean, zid is null, card is null -> label = String(undefined) = "undefined" for each mode. modals.js:88-90 handles pickedMode via pending.effect.options[modeIdx], hence the modal shows 'draw 1'/'channel 1' correctly while the sidebar does not.

findings.what: [Empower] — [1], [Exhaust]: Empower this — activated ability missing
findings.expected: With Egg ready and >=1 energy, an activateAbility move for the Empower ability is offered; activating pays 1 + exhausts and marks the gear Empowered
findings.observed: Turn 3, Egg ready (exhausted=false), energy 3: pw moves lists no activateAbility; direct activateAbility (abilityIndex 0/1/2) returns CONDITION_FAILED. Parser (parseAbilities) returns only {static enters-exhausted} for the full rulesText and 'Could not parse ability text' for the Empower line alone; ven.json abilities is [].
findings.reason: Reproduced with the parser: parseAbilities on Platewyrm Egg's full rulesText returns only {static enters-exhausted}; the Empower line alone returns "Could not parse ability text"; ven.json has abilities: [] / parseSuccess: false. Root cause is riftbound-cards/src/parser/impl/activated.ts:52 — the [Empower] keyword regex `^\[Empower\]\s*(?:—|-)?\s*((?::rb_(...):\s*)+)` only permits whitespace between cost tokens, so the comma-separated cost "[1], [Exhaust]" (normalized ":rb_energy_1:, :rb_exhaust:") fails to match. Verified that "[Empower] — [1][Exhaust]" (no comma) parses to the expected activated {cost:{energy:1,exhaust:true}, effect:empower, restrictions:[not-empowered]}. With no parsed activated ability, no activateAbility move is offered for the card.

findings.what: [Reaction] [Exhaust]: Add [1] (Add [2] instead if Empowered) — activated ability missing / misparsed
findings.expected: With Egg ready, an activateAbility (reaction timing, cost exhaust only) is offered that adds 1 energy (2 if Empowered)
findings.observed: No activateAbility move offered; direct call CONDITION_FAILED. When the line is parsed in isolation the parser yields add-resource energy:3 (sums 1+2) with no Empowered conditional, and in the full multi-line text the ability is dropped entirely. rulesText also contains an HTML-escaped '[>]' token after [Reaction].
findings.reason: Ran getCardRegistry().get("ven-075-166") and parseAbilities() on the card's rulesText: the enriched card carries only [{type:"static",effect:{type:"enters-exhausted"}}] — the [Reaction] [Exhaust]: [Add] activated ability is absent, so no activateAbility move can be offered. Set JSON (packages/riftbound-cards/src/data/sets/ven.json:2352) has abilities:[] / parseSuccess:false and rulesText with the HTML-escaped "[>]"; adaptJsonCard (data/all-cards.ts:805-807) leaves abilities undefined so enrichCard re-parses, and the "[Empower] — [1], [Exhaust] (...)" line fails to parse ("Could not parse ability text"), which takes the following Reaction line down with it (verified: text without the Empower line yields the activated ability; with it, dropped). Parsing line 3 alone hits parser/impl/activated.ts:271-299: addAndMore matches but parseEffect("If this is [Empowered], [Add] :rb_energy_2: instead.") fails, so it falls to parseResourcePayload(resourceText) on the whole tail, and parser/impl/costs.ts:35-38 sums every :rb_energy_N: token → energy:3 with no Empowered conditional.

findings.what: Deathknell trigger never fires when Unsung Hero dies while Mighty
findings.expected: Unsung Hero at 5 Might (base 2 + mightModifier 3) killed by Vengeance (ogn-229-298) should put its Deathknell on the chain and draw 2 (hand 5 -> 7).
findings.observed: Unit moved to trash, no chain item, no pendingChoice, hand stayed at 5. Control test: Watchful Sentry (ogn-096-298, unconditional 'Deathknell — Draw 1') killed by Falling Star also drew nothing, so self 'die' triggers are not firing at all in live play. Code read: trigger-matcher.findMatchingTriggers / trigger-runner.getBoardCards only scan base/battlefield/legendZone; by the time dispatchUnitDied emits `die` the card is already in trash and only `discard` subjects get a trash exemption, so `trigger:{event:'die',on:'self'}` can never match.
findings.reason: Reproduced with the harness: Watchful Sentry (ogn-096-298) and Unsung Hero (sfd-167-221, mightModifier 3) killed by Vengeance both went to trash with 0 cards drawn (deck had 10). Root cause matches the card: abilities/effects/kill.ts:11-21 moves the unit to trash BEFORE calling ctx.fireTriggers({type:'die'}); trigger-runner.ts:333-408 getBoardCards scans only base/legendZone/battlefield-*/battlefieldRow, and trigger-runner.ts:494 only re-adds the subject card for event.type==='discard'; trigger-matcher.ts:352-360 likewise only exempts discard subjects from the on-board zone filter. So a self 'die' trigger can never match in live play. Discriminating check: temporarily extending both the runner push (line 494) and matcher exemption (line 352) to include 'die' made both repro tests pass (Sentry drew 1, Hero drew 2); reverted afterwards. Existing rules-audit Deathknell tests pass only because they fire 'die' while the card is still in base.

findings.what: 'to a minimum of 1 Might' floor is not applied
findings.expected: Targeting a 2-Might unit (Unsung Hero) with Blastcone Fae's play trigger should leave it at 1 Might (modifier effectively -1 / floor at 1).
findings.observed: mightModifier -2 applied, effective Might shown as 0 in the UI (.card-might = '0'). The chain effect carries minimum:1 but the modify-might handler ignores it (no 'minimum' handling anywhere in riftbound-engine effects).
findings.reason: handle_modifyMight (modify-might.ts:7-24) computes `mightModifier: currentMod + amount` with no reference to any `minimum` field; grep for "minimum" under riftbound-engine/src/abilities/ returns nothing. getEffectiveMight (_helpers.ts:79) floors only at Math.max(0, ...). Parser regex (riftbound-cards parser/patterns/effects.ts:74) captures the "to a minimum of N" clause, but the engine never consumes it, so Blastcone Fae's -2 on a 2-Might unit yields effective Might 0 instead of 1.

findings.what: Play-from-Hidden target restriction (rule 811.1.d.2) not enforced
findings.expected: When Blastcone Fae is played from facedown at battlefield player-1-bf-ogn-275-298, the -2 Might target must be chosen from units at that battlefield only (Dangerous Duo).
findings.observed: choose-target pendingChoice options were ['token-recruit-…-0' (in base), 'player-1-main-22-ogn-016-298' (at the battlefield)] — the Recruit token in base was offered as a legal target.
findings.reason: revealHidden reducer (game-definition/moves/play/hide.ts:275-283) clears hidden/hiddenAt meta, then fires a plain `{cardId, playerId, type: "play-self"}` event (hide.ts:337) with no played-from-hidden/battlefield context. Nothing in trigger-runner.ts or target-resolver.ts references hiddenAt or a from-hidden restriction (grep for hiddenAt/fromHidden/811 finds only hide.ts, state-based-checks, scenario). So the play-effect target for Blastcone Fae is resolved with the normal "a unit" filter across all locations, offering base units — rule 811.1.d.2 is not enforced.

findings.what: Blastcone Fae cannot target itself with its own play ability
findings.expected: 'give a unit -2 Might' (not 'another unit') — per rule 355.9.c a permanent's ability may target that permanent, so Fae (2 Might -> 1) should appear among the options.
findings.observed: With Fae + one other unit on board the effect auto-resolved onto the other unit with no prompt; with Fae + two other units the choose-target options listed only the two other units. Fae was never offered.
findings.reason: target-resolver.ts:230-233 unconditionally drops the source card from every non-`self` target set (`if (target.type !== "self") filtered = filtered.filter(id => id !== ctx.sourceCardId)`), with no excludeSelf/"another" gating. The triggered-ability choose-target pool in game-definition/moves/chain/resolve.ts:129-143 enumerates options via resolveTarget({...target, quantity:"all"}, {sourceCardId: resolved.cardId, ...}), so Blastcone Fae's "give a unit -2 Might" (card def has no 'another' qualifier; blastcone-fae.ts:14) never includes Fae itself: with one other unit options.length==1 auto-resolves (resolve.ts:173 requires >=2 to prompt), with two others only those two are listed. This contradicts rule 355.9.c ("An ability of a permanent can target that permanent").

findings.what: Hold trigger ignores the 'exactly one other unit you control here' condition
findings.expected: When Shen holds, score 1 point ONLY if there is exactly one other friendly unit at that battlefield; with 0 other friendly units (Shen alone, or Shen + only enemy tokens) no bonus point should be scored.
findings.observed: With Shen alone at Aspirant's Climb (Punching Poro moved back to base), the hold trigger still went on the chain as an unconditional {type:'score',amount:1} and resolved: VP went 4 -> 5 (hold point + Shen point). Same again next turn with Shen + 3 enemy tokens and 0 friendly units (VP 5 -> 6 + trigger queued). Parser output for the text is condition {type:'exists-here', target:{controller:'friendly',type:'unit',location:'here'}} — an 'any friendly unit here' check (which Shen himself satisfies) instead of count(other friendly units here) == 1.
findings.reason: Parser: riftbound-cards/src/parser/parsers/condition-parser.ts:760-770 matches "there is exactly one other unit you control here" via /^there (?:is|are) (?:a |an )?(.+?)\s+here$/ and buildControlTarget (line 152-156) reduces the subject to a generic {controller:'friendly',type:'unit'} — the "exactly one" count and "other" (excludeSelf) are dropped, yielding condition {type:'exists-here', target:{controller:'friendly',type:'unit',location:'here'}} (verified by running parseAbilities on the card text). Engine: riftbound-engine/src/abilities/trigger-runner.ts evaluateTriggerCondition (lines 166-235) has no branch for 'exists-here' and falls through to `return true` at line 234, so the hold trigger is unconditional and scores 1 even with Shen alone.

findings.what: Self cost reduction 'I cost [2] less for each card with my name in your trash' is not applied
findings.expected: With 1 Shadowblade Lurker in trash the card should be playable for 3 energy; with 2 in trash for 1 energy.
findings.observed: With 1 Lurker in trash (server state shows trash card name 'Shadowblade Lurker', definitionId ven-096-166): playUnit not offered at 3 or 4 energy, only at 5; playing it deducted the full 5 energy (5 -> 0). With 2 Lurkers in trash (one a real killed instance, one duplicate): not playable at 1 or 3 energy, only at 5, and again charged 5. Parser emits {type:'static', effect:{type:'cost-reduction', target:'self', reduction:':rb_energy_2:', scope:'for each card with my name in your trash'}} but the engine has no path that applies a self-targeted, trash-count-scaled static reduction to a card in hand (static-cost-reduction.ts explicitly skips the played card / self-target shapes).
findings.reason: No engine path applies a self-targeted, trash-count-scaled static cost reduction. cost.ts canAffordCard/deductCost (lines 634-646, 726-737) compute energy from registry.getCostToDeduct (card-lookup.ts ~325: printed energyCost only) + meta costModifier + board statics. computeStaticCostReduction (static-cost-reduction.ts:183) explicitly `continue`s when permId === playedCardId, only scans board zones (base/legend/champion/battlefield, never hand), and matchesPlayedCard returns false for string target "self" (static-cost-reduction.ts:349-351). costModifier is only written by the triggered handle_costReduction effect handler (abilities/effects/cost-reduction.ts), never from a static on a card in hand. No code anywhere in riftbound-engine/src references "my name"/trash-name counting for cost. Additionally the shipped card def in riftbound-cards/src/data/sets/ven.json has `abilities: [null]` for ven-096-166. So Shadowblade Lurker is always charged its printed 5.

findings.what: Karma's 'When you recycle one or more cards to your Main Deck, buff a friendly unit' trigger never fires
findings.expected: After a card is recycled to the Main Deck (via Karma's own Vision recycle, and again via Called Shot's 'recycle the other'), a triggered ability should go on the chain / resolve and a friendly unit (Karma, the only friendly unit) should get a +1 Might buff (buffed=true, might 7)
findings.observed: Both recycles happened (Called Shot moved to deck bottom via Vision; Shipyard Skulker moved to deck bottom via Called Shot) but no chain item, no prompt, Karma meta.buffed stayed false and might stayed 6. Parser emits trigger event 'recycle-cards-to-deck' but the engine never emits any recycle game event (no references to 'recycle-cards-to-deck' or a 'recycle' trigger event in riftbound-engine/src).
findings.reason: Parser maps Karma's text to trigger event "recycle-cards-to-deck" (riftbound-cards/src/parser/impl/trigger-patterns.ts:63), but the engine's GameEvent union (riftbound-engine/src/abilities/game-events.ts:11-48) and EVENT_MAP (riftbound-engine/src/abilities/trigger-matcher.ts:67-94) contain no recycle event, and grep for "recycle-cards-to-deck" in riftbound-engine/src returns nothing. recycle.ts / look.ts effects move cards to deck bottom without firing any trigger event, so Karma's triggered buff can never fire.

findings.what: Friendship gives +0 Might with two Poro units (Pouty Poro, Mystic Poro) on my board
findings.expected: Target unit gets +1 Might this turn (one distinct tag — Poro — among my units): Shipyard Skulker 3 -> 4, or Pouty Poro 2 -> 3
findings.observed: Spell resolved to trash, target's mightModifier = 0, might unchanged (Skulker stayed 3; second cast on Pouty Poro stayed 2). Two causes seen in source: (a) Poro unit card data has tags: [] (e.g. ogn-013-298 Pouty Poro, ogn-171-298 Mystic Poro) so no unit ever matches tag 'Poro'; (b) the ability's count filter [{tag:Bird},{tag:Cat},{tag:Dog},{tag:Poro}] is evaluated with filters.every(...) (AND) in target-resolver, so even correctly-tagged units would need all four tags to count, and it counts units rather than distinct tags.
findings.reason: Both causes verified in source. (a) Poro units carry no tags: riftbound-cards/src/cards/ogn/pouty-poro.ts has no `tags` field at all and data/sets/ogn.json has `"tags": []` for ogn-013-298, so matchesFilter's tag check (target-resolver.ts:364-366 `tags?.includes(filter.tag) ?? false`) never matches 'Poro'. (b) friendship.ts:21-25 encodes amount as `count: {type:'unit', controller:'friendly', filter:[{tag:Bird},{tag:Cat},{tag:Dog},{tag:Poro}]}`; evaluated via effects/_helpers.ts:141-151 -> resolveTarget, which at target-resolver.ts:227 applies `filters.every(...)` (AND), so a unit would need all four tags to count. It also counts units not distinct tags (and with no quantity:'all', resolveTarget slices to at most 1 at line 250-251). Net result: amount = 0, +0 Might, matching observed behavior.

findings.what: 'While I'm buffed' condition is not re-evaluated when the buff is removed — Ganking persists after the buff is spent
findings.expected: After Wildclaw Shaman's on-play spent Bilgewater Bully's buff (meta.buffed=false), Bully should lose [Ganking]; gankingMove should not be enumerated and battlefield->battlefield movement should be rejected
findings.observed: meta.buffed=false but meta.grantedKeywords still contains {keyword:'Ganking',duration:'static'} across several subsequent moves/cleanups; gankingMove was still enumerated and executing it moved the unbuffed Bully from battlefield-player-1 to battlefield-player-2 successfully
findings.reason: Static-duration keyword grants are only stripped/re-evaluated inside recalculateStaticEffects (abilities/static-abilities.ts:546), which runs only from performCleanup (cleanup/state-based-checks.ts:292), fireTriggers on play-self (abilities/trigger-runner.ts:477-488), and chain resolve (moves/chain/resolve.ts:322,368). Wildclaw Shaman's "you may spend a buff" is optional, so executeResolvedItem parks it as an `opt-in` pendingChoice (resolve.ts:44-69) and the post-resolve cleanup runs while Bully is still buffed. On accept, resolvePendingChoice (pending-choice.ts:416-440) calls executeResolvedItem -> handle_spendBuff sets buffed=false, but never calls cleanupAndFireDeaths/recalc afterwards. Subsequent moves (standardMove, gankingMove, endTurn) also never recalc: withPostMoveCleanup (cleanup/post-move-cleanup.ts:97) is defined but applied nowhere, and dispatchEvent is not called from any move. gankingMove.condition (moves/movement/ganking-move.ts:49-54) reads the stale meta.grantedKeywords via hasKeyword. Reproduced with the real RuleEngine: after recalc granted {Ganking,static} with buffed=true, setting buffed=false then executing standardMove left grantedKeywords intact, gankingMove was enumerated as valid, and executing it moved the unbuffed unit battlefield-bf-1 -> battlefield-bf-2 successfully.

findings.what: gankingMove is offered and executable while the chain is non-empty (not Neutral Open), unlike standardMove
findings.expected: Ganking uses the unit's Standard Move (rule 144.4.c.1), a Discretionary Action (420.3) legal only in Neutral Open state; with Wallop (and later Wildclaw Shaman's trigger) pending on the chain, no move action should be available (standardMove correctly was not listed)
findings.observed: With Wallop spell on the chain, moves listed gankingMove for Bully; executing it moved Bully bf2->bf1 (exhausted) while the spell was still unresolved on the chain. gankingMove condition lacks the getTurnState(interaction)==='neutral-open' check that standard-move.ts has
findings.reason: ganking-move.ts condition (lines 21-57) and enumerator (lines 58-113) check only pendingChoice/status/activePlayer/phase/zone/owner/exhausted/Ganking keyword; there is no getTurnState(interaction) !== "neutral-open" gate. standard-move.ts:47-52 has exactly that gate ("Standard Move is a Discretionary Action, legal only in a Neutral Open state (no chain, no showdown)"). No central wrapper gates gankingMove elsewhere (only referenced in movement.ts export, bot weights, harness). So gankingMove is offered/executable with items on the chain.

findings.what: Firestorm does not ask for a battlefield and damages enemy units at every battlefield
findings.expected: 'Deal 3 to all enemy units at a battlefield' — player should choose one battlefield; only enemy units at that battlefield take 3 damage
findings.observed: playSpell offered no target/battlefield parameter and no pendingChoice; chain effect target was {type:unit,controller:enemy,quantity:all,location:'battlefield'} and on resolution enemy Mechs at BOTH battlefields (battlefield-player-2-bf-ogn-276-298 and battlefield-player-1-bf-ogn-277-298) were killed. Enemy unit in base and friendly unit at the battlefield were correctly untouched.
findings.reason: target-resolver.ts:217-221 filters `location:"battlefield"` to any zone starting with "battlefield" (no single-battlefield pin), and :246-247 returns every match for quantity:"all". play-spell.ts:330-336 sets isCardTarget=false when quantity==="all", falling to :536-540 which pushes a Play variant with no targets and no battlefield choice. Firestorm (riftbound-cards/src/cards/ogs/firestorm.ts) has no explicit abilities override, so "Deal 3 to all enemy units at a battlefield" hits enemy units at every battlefield with no player choice.

findings.what: Lethal-damage state-based check ignores might modifiers (observed while testing Firestorm)
findings.expected: An enemy Mech with +2 might (3 base + 2 mightModifier = 5) taking 3 damage should survive with 3 damage marked
findings.observed: It died. Reproduced in isolation with sandbox modifyBuff +2 then addDamage 3 on a Mech -> unit removed. cleanup/state-based-checks.ts compares damage against registry base might only (def.might), not effective might.
findings.reason: cleanup/state-based-checks.ts:164-173 reads `const baseMight = def?.might ?? 0` from the global card registry and kills when `damage >= baseMight`; meta.mightModifier is never consulted (only reset to 0 on death at lines 197/264). A 3-might Mech with +2 modifier and 3 damage satisfies 3 >= 3 and is killed.

findings.what: Megatusk's 'Give your units here [Ganking] this turn' excludes Megatusk itself
findings.expected: All friendly units at Megatusk's location, INCLUDING Megatusk (reminder text: 'We can move from battlefield to battlefield'), receive Ganking this turn
findings.observed: After activation+resolve (twice: once in base, once on a battlefield), only the other unit (Legion Rearguard) got meta.grantedKeywords=[Ganking]; Megatusk's meta had no grantedKeywords and no gankingMove was offered for Megatusk while gankingMove WAS offered for Legion Rearguard. Cause: target-resolver.ts unconditionally filters out ctx.sourceCardId for any non-'self' target (line ~230 'Exclude self'), so quantity:'all' friendly/here effects never include the source.
findings.reason: target-resolver.ts:230-233 unconditionally drops ctx.sourceCardId for any target whose type !== "self" (`if (target.type !== "self") filtered = filtered.filter(id => id !== ctx.sourceCardId)`), ignoring the descriptor's excludeSelf flag. Megatusk (unl-126-219, cards/unl/megatusk.ts) has no explicit abilities; its rulesText "Give your units here [Ganking] this turn" is parsed by effects-grant-keyword.ts:40-69 into {controller:"friendly", type:"unit", quantity:"all", location:"here"} with NO excludeSelf (excludeSelf is only set when "other" is present, line 56-58). resolveTarget (used by effects/_helpers.ts et al.) therefore excludes Megatusk from its own "your units here" grant, contradicting the card's reminder text ("We can move..."). Other engine paths (static-abilities.ts:393, trigger-runner.ts:283) correctly gate on t.excludeSelf, but target-resolver does not.

findings.what: Acceleration Gate resolves with no effect — nothing is readied and no target prompt is shown
findings.expected: On play/resolve, a choice of up to 4 exhausted units, gear and/or runes, which become ready
findings.observed: With 3 exhausted friendly units in base and 2 exhausted runes, playSpell put a chain item with no effect/targets; after passChainPriority the spell went to trash (trash=1) and all 3 units and both runes remained exhausted; no pendingChoice, no per-target moves. Enriched card def (getAllCards) has no 'abilities' at all — set JSON parseSuccess=false, abilities=[] and the rulesText re-parse produces nothing for 'Ready up to 4 units, gear, and/or runes.'
findings.reason: Card def at /root/src/tcg/tcg-engines/packages/riftbound-cards/src/data/sets/ven.json:4257 (ven-150-166 Acceleration Gate) has "abilities": [], "parseSuccess": false — no effect defined. The only reference to the id in riftbound-cards/src is that JSON entry (no TS override). Re-parsing the rulesText fails: running parseAbilities("Ready up to 4 units, gear, and/or runes.") returns {success:false, error:"Could not parse ability text"} because READY_PATTERN at riftbound-cards/src/parser/patterns/effects.ts:413 only allows `(?:\w+\s+)*?` word modifiers before the type noun and cannot match the comma/"and/or" mixed-type list "units, gear, and/or runes". With no abilities, the spell resolves as a no-op (no targets, nothing readied), matching the observed behavior.

findings.what: Hybrid mind/body power pip was paid with Fury power
findings.expected: The 1 power pip of a mind/body dual-domain card should only be payable with mind, body, or universal (rainbow) power
findings.observed: Pool before play: rainbow1 fury3 chaos2 mind2 body2; after playSpell: fury 3->2 with mind/body/rainbow untouched. Card registry models the hybrid pip as powerCost:['rainbow'] (derivePowerCost in all-cards.ts maps every multi-domain card to rainbow = any domain), so off-domain power is accepted.
findings.reason: packages/riftbound-cards/src/data/all-cards.ts:860 — derivePowerCost maps any multi-domain card (ven-150-166 domains=[mind,body], power=1) to powerCost ['rainbow']. The engine then treats that pip as Rule 135.2.e.5.a "any Domain": cost.ts:682-706 (canAfford sums all leftover domains) and cost.ts:757-779 (deductCost drains rainbowOwed from whichever domain has the most Power — fury=3 in the observed pool, hence fury 3->2). Rule 135.2.e.6.c states a multi-domain card's [C] power cost is payable only with Power of that card's own Domains (example: Defiant Dance Calm/Chaos payable with [G] or [P] only), so accepting Fury for a Mind/Body pip is wrong. MULTI_DOMAIN_POWER_OVERRIDES (all-cards.ts:845) is empty, so no per-card correction exists.

findings.what: Legion clause not implemented — target is not killed immediately when another card was played earlier this turn
findings.expected: With 3 units already played this turn (Legion satisfied), Noxian Guillotine targeting Mystic Poro should kill Poro on resolution
findings.observed: Spell resolved to trash, Poro remained in base undamaged. Runtime ability (from /api/cards/ogn-254-298) has only a single replacement effect and no Legion/conditional branch at all
findings.reason: Card def /root/src/tcg/tcg-engines/packages/riftbound-cards/src/cards/ogn/noxian-guillotine.ts:4-16 has no `abilities` field, so enrich-cards.ts:29 derives them via parseAbilities(rulesText). Running the parser on the exact rulesText yields exactly one ability: {type:"spell", timing:"action", effect:{type:"replacement", replaces:"take-damage", duration:"next", replacement:{type:"kill", target:{type:"unit"}}}} — no Legion/conditional branch. Cause: parser/index.ts:106 returns the single-ability result early for text starting with [Action] (no raw effect, no [Repeat]), dropping the trailing "[Legion] — Kill it now instead." clause. Hence with Legion satisfied the target is never killed on resolution.

findings.what: Base clause 'Kill it the next time it takes damage this turn' does nothing
findings.expected: After Guillotine resolved targeting Zephyr Sage (6 Might), a subsequent Falling Star dealing 3 to Sage the same turn should kill it
findings.observed: Sage took the damage (meta.damage=3) and stayed alive. Reproduced twice: once on a Legion turn and once on turn 3 with Guillotine as the first card played (non-Legion path). The 'replacement: take-damage -> kill, duration next' effect is never applied/consulted
findings.reason: Guillotine's base clause parses to a spell effect {type:"replacement", replaces:"take-damage", duration:"next", replacement:{kill}} (riftbound-cards/src/parser/impl/replacement.ts:133-149). On resolve, handle_replacement (riftbound-engine/src/abilities/effects/replacement.ts:5-27) merely appends it to draft.activeReplacements — and only binds targetCardIds when replaces==="die" (line 15), so the chosen unit isn't even recorded for take-damage. The damage path never consults that entry: handle_damage (abilities/effects/damage.ts:16-32) only reads activeReplacements for the global prevent-all case (replacement==="prevent" && global && amount==="all"), then calls checkReplacement (abilities/replacement-effects.ts:239-314), which scans only static `type:"replacement"` abilities on cards currently in base/battlefield zones via the registry — a resolved spell in trash with a `type:"spell"` ability is never matched. The only other activeReplacements consumers handle "die" (cleanup/state-based-checks.ts:107-124) and "enters-ready" (moves/play/cost.ts:174+). So a runtime take-damage->kill replacement is installed but never applied; subsequent damage just accrues to meta.damage, matching the observed behavior.

findings.what: 'Choose a unit' — no target prompt; spell is castable with no target
findings.expected: Playing the spell should require choosing a unit (per-target playSpell moves or a pendingChoice), and should not be castable with zero units on board
findings.observed: playSpell for Guillotine is enumerated with no `targets` param (unlike Dancing Grenade/Falling Star which list per-target moves); clicking the card in hand with 3 units on board put it straight on the chain with no targets; it was also castable (paid 4 energy + 1 power) with an empty board and simply fizzled
findings.reason: Guillotine's runtime ability is parser-derived (riftbound-cards/src/data/enrich-cards.ts:29) as `{type:"spell", effect:{type:"replacement", replaces:"take-damage", duration:"next", replacement:{type:"kill", target:{type:"unit"}}}}` — the unit target lives only inside the nested `replacement`, with no top-level `effect.target`. In play-spell.ts enumerator (lines 307-336) `tgt = spellEffect.target ?? refTgt ?? findSequenceLeadTarget(...)` is undefined for a non-sequence `replacement` effect, so `isCardTarget` is false and it falls to the untargeted branch at play-spell.ts:536-540 (pushes {cardId, playerId} with no targets). The legality gate spellEffectHasLegalTargets (targeting.ts:185-251) only inspects effect.target/target1/target2/attacker/defender — all undefined here — and returns true, so the condition at play-spell.ts:172-179 passes on an empty board. At resolution, handle_replacement (abilities/effects/replacement.ts:5-27) just appends to activeReplacements without prompting a pendingChoice (targetCardIds only bound for replaces==="die"). Hence no target prompt and castable with zero units.

findings.what: Recruit tokens are always created in base; no option to play them to a controlled battlefield
findings.expected: Reminder text: 'They can be played to your base or to battlefields you control' (rules 439.2.b.1/184.2). With player-1 controlling battlefield ogn-277-298 (controller=player-1, and playUnit moves for hand units offered that battlefield as a location), casting Recruit the Vanguard should offer a location choice per token (or at least base vs battlefield)
findings.observed: No pendingChoice/location prompt; all four tokens created directly in base both times (with and without a controlled battlefield)
findings.reason: riftbound-engine/src/abilities/effects/create-token.ts:69-76 — when effect.location is undefined (parser at riftbound-cards/src/parser/impl/effects-tokens.ts:101-115 only sets location for explicit 'here'/'base' suffixes; "Play four 1 [Might] Recruit unit tokens." has none), handle_createToken falls to `targetZone = "base"` and calls ctx.createCardInZone(tokenId, "base", ...) for every token (line 108). No pendingChoice/location selection exists anywhere in the create-token path, so controlled battlefields are never offered, contrary to rule 439.2.b.1 ("Permanents will be Created at any location on the Board that they can be played to") and the card's reminder text.

findings.what: "Then, if there's an enemy unit alone at that battlefield, draw 1" clause is not implemented
findings.expected: After moving one of two enemy Recruits from Back-Alley Bar to base, the remaining enemy Recruit is alone at that battlefield, so player-1 should draw 1 (hand 5->6, deck 35->34)
findings.observed: No draw: hand stayed at 5, player-1 mainDeck stayed at 35. Chain item effect was only {type:move,target:{unit,enemy},to:base}; parseAbilities() output for this rulesText has no conditional/draw follow-up at all
findings.reason: isolate.ts:4-16 defines unl-124-219 with only rulesText and no explicit `abilities`, so it relies on parseAbilities(). Running parseAbilities() on the exact rulesText yields a single spell ability with effect {type:"move", target:{type:"unit",controller:"enemy"}, to:"base"} and nothing else — the "Then, if there's an enemy unit alone at that battlefield, draw 1" clause is silently dropped (no conditional/sequence/draw). No override for this card id exists in riftbound-engine/src or server.ts. Hence no draw occurs after the move.

findings.what: Target is not restricted to enemy units at a battlefield ("from a battlefield")
findings.expected: Only enemy units located at a battlefield should be legal targets; an enemy unit sitting in its base should not be targetable
findings.observed: After the first cast moved token-recruit-player-2-12 to player-2's base, a second Isolate still enumerated that base unit as a legal target (playSpell targets included token-recruit-player-2-12), the engine accepted the cast (energy deducted, chain item created) and resolved it. Parsed target descriptor is {type:unit,controller:enemy} with no location:battlefield
findings.reason: Runtime registry (getCardRegistry().get("unl-124-219").abilities, verified via bun) yields effect {type:"move", target:{type:"unit",controller:"enemy"}, to:"base"} — no location:"battlefield" and no usable `from`. play-spell.ts:432 enumerates caster targets via resolveTarget({...tgt, quantity:"all"}); target-resolver.ts:182-222 only filters by zone when target.location is set, so with location undefined enemy units in base pass. The move executor (abilities/effects/move.ts:69) only consults `from` when it equals "chosen-battlefield". Parser source: riftbound-cards/src/parser/impl/effects-move.ts:60-79 (and parsers/effect-parser.ts:97-116) capture "from a battlefield" into a separate `from` field rather than target.location, which the engine ignores. So an enemy unit in its base is a legal Isolate target.

findings.what: "Move a friendly unit" gives no destination choice; move is hard-coded to base
findings.expected: Per rule 355.4/355.4.a (whose example text literally cites Ride the Wind), the caster chooses a valid destination (base or a battlefield) for the moved unit; a unit at base should be movable to a battlefield
findings.observed: Parsed effect is {type:move,target:{unit,friendly},to:'base'}. Casting on an exhausted unit at a battlefield moved it straight to base with no pendingChoice/destination prompt. Casting on a unit already at base was allowed and resolved with the unit staying in base (no way to send it to a battlefield)
findings.reason: Parsing "Move a friendly unit and ready it." yields {type:move,target:{unit,friendly},to:"base"} (verified by running parseAbilities). riftbound-cards/src/parser/impl/effects-move.ts:192 (`const to = destStr ? parseLocationString(destStr) : "base"`) and :224 hard-default an absent destination to "base" instead of "choose". Engine handle_move (riftbound-engine/src/abilities/effects/move.ts:225-253) only raises a choose-destination pendingChoice when to === "choose"; for to:"base" it falls to move.ts:259-266 and moves directly to base. Rule 355.4/355.4.a require the caster to pick any valid location other than current, so a unit at base can never be sent to a battlefield.

findings.what: "spend 3 XP" cost is not enforced on the attack trigger
findings.expected: With fewer than 3 XP the optional ability should not be usable (or should fizzle); accepting must deduct 3 XP before dealing damage
findings.observed: With player-1 XP=2, resolvePendingChoice{accept:true} was still offered; accepting dealt 5 damage to the enemy Mystic Poro and XP stayed at 2 (nothing spent)
findings.reason: Card unl-119-219 has no explicit abilities; enrich-cards.ts parses rulesText into an optional attack trigger with effect sequence [{type:"spend-xp",amount:3},{type:"damage",...}]. Engine gaps: (1) abilities/effects/spend-xp.ts:8-10 — handle_spendXp silently no-ops when player.xp < amount (no abort/fizzle signal). (2) abilities/effects/sequence.ts:80 — the sequence handler only gates remaining steps on an unpayable `spend-buff` lead (findSpendableBuff); there is no equivalent check for `spend-xp`, so the damage step runs regardless. (3) game-definition/moves/chain/resolve.ts:53-61 — the opt-in prompt suppression for unpayable optional costs likewise only checks leadEffect.type === "spend-buff", so with XP=2 the opt-in choice is still offered. Result matches observation: prompt offered, accept deals Might damage, XP unchanged.

findings.what: No target selection for "an enemy unit here" when multiple enemy units are present
findings.expected: A choose-target prompt (pendingChoice / per-target moves) letting the controller pick which enemy unit at the battlefield takes the damage
findings.observed: With 2 enemy units at the battlefield (Noxus Saboteur + Legion Rearguard; also 2 Mech tokens) the only prompt was the Yes/No opt-in; on accept the engine auto-damaged the first enemy unit in the zone with no choice offered
findings.reason: Kha'Zix parses to an optional triggered ability whose effect is `{type:"sequence", effects:[{type:"spend-xp",amount:3},{type:"damage",amount:{might:"self"},target:{type:"unit",controller:"enemy",location:"here"}}]}` (no top-level `target`). At resolution, game-definition/moves/chain/resolve.ts:114-186 only raises a `choose-target` pendingChoice when `effect.target` exists on the top-level effect; a `sequence` has none, so it falls straight to executeEffect (resolve.ts:213). abilities/effects/sequence.ts:76-188 has no choose-target path for an unbound card-descriptor sub-step (only same-location/pending-value/slot routing), so handle_damage (abilities/effects/damage.ts:176) calls getTargetIds → resolveTarget, which with no quantity returns `filtered.slice(0, 1)` (abilities/target-resolver.ts:250-251) — the first enemy unit in the zone, no prompt. Only the opt-in prompt (resolve.ts:62-68) is shown.

findings.what: Unit given lethal damage by Kha'Zix's attack ability is not killed (no state-based check after opt-in resolution)
findings.expected: Per rule 143.2.a / cleanup 319.5, a unit whose damage >= Might is killed immediately after the ability resolves, before combat damage
findings.observed: Noxus Saboteur (Might 3) sat on the battlefield with damage=5 (also Mystic Poro Might 2 dmg 5, Mech token Might 3 dmg 5) through passShowdownFocus; it still counted as a defender in resolveFullCombat, contributing its Might so Kha'Zix (5) took 5 and died. pending-choice.ts opt-in accept path calls executeResolvedItem without running cleanup (chain/resolve.ts does; withPostMoveCleanup is defined but never applied)
findings.reason: pending-choice.ts:416-441 — the `opt-in` accept branch calls `executeResolvedItem(choice.resolved, draft, context)` and returns with no state-based check; by contrast chain/resolve.ts:316-322 and 364-368 follow executeResolvedItem with `cleanupAndFireDeaths(draft, context)`. No branch of resolvePendingChoice (opt-in, choose-target, choose-mode, ...) calls performCleanup/cleanupAndFireDeaths (grep: zero hits in pending-choice.ts). `withPostMoveCleanup` (cleanup/post-move-cleanup.ts:97) is defined but referenced nowhere else, and events/dispatcher.ts `dispatchEvent`/`runStateMaintenance` are only imported by that unused wrapper. abilities/effects/damage.ts:163/242 only adds a "damage" counter and never kills. resolve-full-combat.ts:114-181 builds defenderUnits from every unit in the battlefield zone using currentDamage/baseMight with no pre-combat lethal reaping, so a Might-3 unit carrying 5 damage from Kha'Zix's optional (opt-in) attack trigger survives and contributes Might in combat.

findings.what: "Opponents can't play cards this turn" is not enforced
findings.expected: After Brynhir's play trigger resolves, player-2 should have no playSpell/playUnit moves for the rest of the turn and any attempt should be rejected
findings.observed: After the trigger resolved, player-1 cast Stacked Deck and passed priority; player-2's moves still listed playSpell Discipline and executing it succeeded ('Goldfish cast Discipline' on the chain, p2 energy 6->4) in the same turn. The grant-keyword effect (target player/opponent) instead attached grantedKeywords:[{keyword:'CannotPlayCards',duration:'turn'}] to Brynhir's own card meta; no player-level restriction exists (card file comment admits engine support pending)
findings.reason: The string "CannotPlayCards" appears nowhere in riftbound-engine/src or server.ts (grep returns zero hits) — no play move consults it, so no player-level play restriction can exist. The card (riftbound-cards/src/cards/ogn/brynhir-thundersong.ts:17-22) emits grant-keyword with target {type:"player"}; handle_grantKeyword (abilities/effects/grant-keyword.ts:12-13) gets no card ids for a player target and falls back to `[ctx.sourceCardId]`, then writes grantedKeywords onto Brynhir's own card meta (lines 15-26), exactly matching the observed state. Card file comment (lines 10-13) acknowledges engine support is pending.

findings.what: Discard resolves against the wrong player
findings.expected: "They discard 1" — the chosen player (default/only sensible target here: the opponent, and the chain item itself said effect.player="opponent") discards a card from THEIR hand; player-2 hand should go 4→3.
findings.observed: On resolution a reveal-and-pick pendingChoice was created with prompter=revealer=player-1 listing player-1's own hand; after picking, player-1's Detonate went to player-1 trash (hand 6→5) while player-2's hand stayed at 4. handle_discard in riftbound-engine/src/abilities/effects/discard.ts ignores effect.player==='opponent' and always uses ctx.playerId.
findings.reason: Parser (riftbound-cards/src/parser/impl/effects-draw.ts:159-164) emits {type:"discard", player:"opponent", amount:1} for "They discard 1". handle_discard (riftbound-engine/src/abilities/effects/discard.ts:11-12, 29-45) only special-cases player==="each" or amount==="hand"; otherwise it reads the hand via ctx.zones.getCardsInZone("hand", ctx.playerId) and sets pendingChoice prompter/revealer = ctx.playerId, never consulting effect.player==="opponent". executeEffect (effect-executor.ts:145-152) dispatches directly with no player remapping. So the controller discards from their own hand.

findings.what: No 'choose a player' prompt
findings.expected: rulesText says 'choose a player' — controller should be prompted to pick self or opponent before the discard.
findings.observed: Parser emits {type:discard, amount:1, player:'opponent'} with no player-choice step; no pendingChoice/target prompt was shown when the trigger went on the chain.
findings.reason: Card def bewitching-spirit.ts has no explicit abilities, so it relies on the parser. Running parseAbilities("When you play me, choose a player. They discard 1.") yields {type:"triggered", trigger:{event:"play-self"}, effect:{type:"discard", amount:1, player:"opponent"}} — no player-choice step. Mechanism: effects.ts:173-190 splits sentences and silently drops "choose a player." (parseEffect returns undefined for it), then effects-draw.ts:159-164 matches /^(?:They|that player) discards? .../ and hard-codes player:"opponent". The parser's own test (parser/__tests__/effects/discard.test.ts:319-330) asserts this opponent-only output. Engine side, abilities/effects/discard.ts only handles player "each" or defaults to ctx.playerId; there is no choose-player prompt anywhere (no grep hits for a player-choice pendingChoice). So the controller is never prompted to pick self vs opponent as the rules text requires.

findings.what: Granted [Repeat] [2][chaos] is never offered on spells while Syndra is in a showdown
findings.expected: With Syndra at the showdown battlefield (showdown.active=true, focusPlayer=player-1) and 9 energy + 1 chaos power, playing Stacked Deck (cost 1) should offer a playSpell variant with repeatCount:1 (pay +[2][chaos]) and resolve the look effect twice.
findings.observed: pw moves listed only the base playSpell (no repeatCount variant); executeMove playSpell with repeatCount:1 was rejected (card stayed in hand, energy unchanged); base cast resolved the effect exactly once. Parser turns the text into a static grant-keyword Repeat targeting friendly *units* with no cost and no in-showdown condition, and engine getSpellRepeatCost/play-spell enumerator only read the spell definition's intrinsic repeat tiers, so a granted Repeat can never apply.
