findings.reason: Parser (verified by running parseAbilities on the rules text) yields a static grant-keyword Repeat with target {type:unit, controller:friendly}, no cost and no showdown condition. Engine: CardDefinitionRegistry.getSpellRepeatCost (riftbound-engine/src/operations/card-lookup.ts:219-236) only reads `ab.repeat` on the spell card's own spell ability; play-spell.ts:74-84 returns false for repeatCount>0 when that is undefined, and the enumerator at play-spell.ts:583 uses the same intrinsic tiers; cost.ts:541/568 likewise. grep finds no granted-Repeat handling anywhere in riftbound-engine/src. So Syndra's granted [Repeat][2][chaos] can never be offered or paid.

findings.what: Turn-scoped +3 Might modifier persisted on Teemo while it was off-board (hand / facedown zone) and stacked when replayed from Hidden
findings.expected: After playing Teemo from facedown on turn 3, might should be 1 base + 3 (play trigger) = 4; the +3 'this turn' from the turn-1 play should be gone (turn ended, and card changed zones board->hand->facedown)
findings.observed: meta.mightModifier was still 3 while facedown at end of turn 1 and start of turn 3; after revealHidden + trigger resolution mightModifier=6 and UI showed Effective Might 7. End-of-turn cleanup in riftbound-flow only iterates base + battlefield-* zones (facedown-*/hand skipped) and return-to-hand / hideCard zone moves do not reset mightModifier. (Repro used debug sendToHand for the bounce step; abilities/effects/return-to-hand.ts likewise does a bare moveCard with no meta reset, so a real bounce->hide line reaches the same state.)
findings.reason: End-of-turn expiration in game-definition/flow/riftbound-flow.ts:556-609 builds allBoardCards only from "base" and "battlefield-*" zones and resets mightModifier only for those (line 606-608); cards in hand / facedown-* zones are never touched. abilities/effects/return-to-hand.ts:14-24 does a bare ctx.zones.moveCard to hand with no meta reset; hideCard (game-definition/moves/play/hide.ts:168-183) only sets hidden/hiddenAt/hiddenOnTurn; revealHidden (hide.ts:276-283, 317-341) clears only hidden flags then fires play-self, so Teemo's "+3 Might this turn" (modify-might.ts:15-19 adds to currentMod) stacks on the stale 3 -> 6. Core moveCard (core/src/operations/operations-impl.ts:174-251) does not touch cardMetas, and state-based-checks.ts only zeroes mightModifier on kill/banish paths (lines 197, 264), not on bounce.

findings.what: Hidden (facedown) card is not rendered anywhere on the board for its owner
findings.expected: After hideCard, the controlling player should see a facedown card at Back-Alley Bar (facedown-player-1-bf-ogn-277-298 zone) so they know it is there and can play it later
findings.observed: Engine state has Teemo in zone facedown-player-1-bf-ogn-277-298 with hidden:true, but the battlefield DOM contains only Gust Monk; no element references the card id or any facedown-* zone (public/js/gameplay never reads facedown-* zones). Only the sidebar 'Reveal Hidden - Teemo, Scout' action button reveals its existence.
findings.reason: Engine stores hidden cards in `facedown-${bfId}` zones (e.g. cleanup/state-based-checks.ts:299, operations/player-removal.ts:115). The UI battlefield renderer at apps/riftbound-app/public/js/gameplay/render/board.js:89-90 only reads `zones[\`battlefield-${bfId}\`]` and renders opponentUnits/playerUnits from that; grep across public/js/gameplay finds zero references to any `facedown-` zone key (the only 'facedown' hits are card.js:128/137 CSS-class stand-ins for opponent/hand-hidden cards, unrelated to the facedown zone). So a card moved by hideCard into facedown-<bf> is never rendered on the board.

findings.what: XP gained is never displayed in the play UI
findings.expected: After 'When you play me, gain 2 XP' (and Hunt) resolve, the player's XP total (2, then 3, then 4) is visible somewhere on the board — at minimum when the 'XP Counter' board toggle is switched On
findings.observed: Server snapshot/REST state shows players.player-1.xp going 0->2->3->4 correctly, but no element in the DOM renders XP; toggling data-toggle-name=xpCounter to aria-pressed=true changes nothing (public/js only references xpCounter in board-toggles.js, no renderer consumes it)
findings.reason: The only references to XP in the play UI are in board-toggles.js (lines 16, 33-35, 54-56), which merely persists the xpCounter toggle to localStorage; the file's own header comment (lines 4-8) states the toggles are "read by future workstreams" with "no renderer coupling". grep for `xp`/`xpCounter` across public/js/gameplay/render/, public/*.html, and the rest of public/js returns no consumer — no renderer reads player xp state or the xpCounter toggle. Card herald-of-spring.ts (unl-034-219) has "When you play me, gain 2 XP" + Hunt, so XP changes in engine state are never surfaced in the DOM.

findings.what: Imperial Decree's 'When any unit takes damage this turn, kill it' does nothing
findings.expected: After Decree resolves, any unit that takes damage this turn is killed — e.g. enemy Mech token (3 might) taking 2 from Incinerate, and friendly Herald of Spring (4 might) taking 3 from Hextech Ray, should both go to trash
findings.observed: Decree resolved to trash and installed {type:replacement, replaces:'take-damage', replacement:{type:'kill'}, duration:'turn'} into draft.activeReplacements, but nothing consumes it: Mech stayed on Altar to Unity with meta.damage=2, Herald stayed on Back-Alley Bar with meta.damage=3; no kill, no chain item, no log entry. handle_damage only checks activeReplacements for the global 'prevent' case; findAllReplacements only scans abilities of cards on board (Decree is a resolved spell in trash). Effect should probably be modelled as a turn-scoped delayed trigger (unit still takes the damage, then is killed) rather than a replacement.
findings.reason: Parser (riftbound-cards/src/parser/impl/replacement.ts:152-168) emits Imperial Decree as {type:'replacement', replaces:'take-damage', duration:'turn', replacement:kill}; on resolve handle_replacement (engine abilities/effects/replacement.ts:9-26) just appends it to draft.activeReplacements. The only consumers of activeReplacements are: damage.ts:16-31 (matches only replacement==='prevent' && global && amount==='all'), state-based-checks.ts:112 (replaces:'die'), cost.ts:178 (cost replacements), prevent-damage.ts, and flow cleanup. The per-hit checkReplacement/findAllReplacements (replacement-effects.ts:108-178, 239-314) scan only abilities of cards in base/battlefield zones via the registry, never draft.activeReplacements, so a resolved spell in trash contributes nothing. No path kills a damaged unit for a take-damage/kill entry — the effect is inert as reported.

findings.what: "double my Might this combat" does not expire at end of combat
findings.expected: Per rule 466.7.c all 'this combat' effects expire when combat ends; Fiora should return to 3 Might after combat resolves and a second one-on-one combat in the same turn should double 3->6 again.
findings.observed: After resolveFullCombat Fiora kept meta.mightModifier=3 (UI Effective Might 6) for the rest of the turn; it only cleared at end of turn. A second solo attacker in the same turn doubled from 6 -> 12 (mightModifier 9), and a third combat took her to 24. Engine handle_doubleMight (abilities/effects/double-might.ts) ignores effect.duration and always writes a turn-scoped mightModifier.
findings.reason: Card def fiora-peerless.ts sets effect {type:"double-might", duration:"combat"}, but handle_doubleMight (abilities/effects/double-might.ts:7-25) never reads effect.duration and writes meta.mightModifier += effectiveMight (line 21), the same turn-scoped field modify-might uses. mightModifier is only reset at Ending Step (flow/riftbound-flow.ts:608) or for killed units (resolve-full-combat.ts:233); survivors keep it after combat cleanup. Only grant-keyword(s).ts honor duration:"combat". So the doubling persists past combat (violating 466.7.c) and compounds 3->6->12->24 on repeat solo combats in one turn.

findings.what: "one on one" condition is not enforced
findings.expected: When two enemy units (Eager Drakehound + Void Drone) moved together to attack Fiora defending alone, the trigger should NOT fire (not one on one); Fiora should fight at 3 Might and die to 6 combined Might.
findings.observed: Defend trigger was put on the chain and resolved, doubling Fiora (12 -> 24); she killed both attackers and survived. evaluateTriggerCondition in abilities/trigger-runner.ts has no case for condition.type 'alone-in-combat' and falls through to permissive `return true`.
findings.reason: fiora-peerless.ts defines condition {type:'alone-in-combat', role:...} on both attack/defend triggers, but `grep -rn alone-in-combat` over riftbound-engine/src returns zero hits. evaluateTriggerCondition (abilities/trigger-runner.ts:166-235) handles only legion, paid-additional-cost, while-empowered, while-at-battlefield, fewer-runes-than-opponent, control, then unconditionally `return true` at line 234 — so Fiora's double-might trigger fires regardless of how many enemy units are in combat.

findings.what: "When you discard one or more cards" triggers once per card instead of once per discard event
findings.expected: A single 'Discard 2' instruction (Jinx, Demolitionist on-play) is one discard of one-or-more cards, so Jinx, Rebel should trigger once: ready + +1 Might (mightModifier 1 -> 2).
findings.observed: Two separate chain items (chain-5, chain-6) were created, one per discarded card (Void Hatchling, Sinister Poro); after resolving both, mightModifier went 1 -> 3 and UI Might showed 8. Engine emits a per-card 'discard' event and the trigger matcher does not batch them.
findings.reason: handle_discard (packages/riftbound-engine/src/abilities/effects/discard.ts:48-52) loops over each auto-discarded card for count>1 and calls ctx.fireTriggers({type:"discard", cardId, ...}) once per card (also lines 20-23 for each/hand branch). The parser maps "When you discard one or more cards" to {event:"discard", on:"controller"} (packages/riftbound-cards/src/parser/impl/trigger-patterns.ts:203) with no batching marker, and fireTriggers/findMatchingTriggers (trigger-runner.ts:475ff, trigger-matcher.ts:340ff) process each event independently with no dedupe/batch logic. So Jinx, Demolitionist's "discard 2" produces two discard events and Jinx, Rebel's controller trigger matches twice, yielding two chain items and +2 Might instead of +1.

findings.what: Static 'Each Equipment attached to me gives double its base Might bonus' is not applied by the engine
findings.expected: With B.F. Sword (mightBonus 3) attached, Gearhead's effective Might should be 3 + 2*3 = 9 (i.e. an extra +3 over the normal equip bonus, e.g. via staticMightBonus=3)
findings.observed: After equipCard succeeded (unit meta.equippedWith=[B.F. Sword], sword meta.attachedTo=Gearhead), Gearhead meta.staticMightBonus stayed 0. Parser emits {type:'modify-might', multiplier:2, source:'equipment'} (static-parser.ts) but static-abilities.ts modify-might handler only reads effect.amount (undefined -> 0) and ignores multiplier/source; getEffectiveMight/_helpers.ts and resolve-full-combat.ts just sum registry.getMightBonus once per equipment, so effective Might is 6 not 9.
findings.reason: static-parser.ts:820-825 emits {type:'modify-might', multiplier:2, source:'equipment'} with no amount. Engine static-abilities.ts:441-477 modify-might handler reads only effect.amount (undefined -> amount=0) and adds 0 to staticMightBonus; grep for 'multiplier' across riftbound-engine/src (non-test) returns zero hits. Equipment bonus is summed once via registry.getMightBonus in abilities/effects/_helpers.ts:74, resolve-full-combat.ts:130, cost.ts:437 with no doubling. So Gearhead's double-equipment-bonus static is never applied.

findings.what: Board card Might display ignores attached Equipment entirely
findings.expected: Gearhead with B.F. Sword attached should show boosted Might (9, or at least 6) on the board card
findings.observed: No .card-might badge rendered; card shows printed 3. render/card.js computes effMight = base + mightModifier + staticMightBonus + buffed with no equippedWith term, and the server snapshot 'might' is the printed value only.
findings.reason: render/card.js:197-203 computes effMight = card.might + meta.mightModifier + meta.staticMightBonus + (meta.buffed?1:0) with no equippedWith/equipment term, and renders .card-might only when effMight !== baseMight. server/snapshot.ts:389 sets might from the printed card def only. Engine keeps equipment bonus as a separate term summed from meta.equippedWith via registry.getMightBonus (abilities/effects/_helpers.ts:72-77, resolve-full-combat.ts:128-138); equipCard reducer (moves/equipment.ts:126-134) only appends to equippedWith and never touches mightModifier/staticMightBonus. So Gearhead (might 3) with B.F. Sword (mightBonus 3) yields effMight==3 in UI, no badge rendered.

findings.what: No targeting prompt for 'Choose a friendly unit that's in combat with an enemy Fury unit'
findings.expected: Playing Decree of Focus should prompt to choose a friendly unit meeting the restriction (pendingChoice or per-target playSpell variants) and put it on the chain with that target
findings.observed: Enumerated playSpell has only {cardId,playerId}; clicking the card in hand (with Gust Monk legally in combat vs a player-2-owned Fury Legion Rearguard) put the spell on the chain with no targets and pendingChoice=null; chain item effect is {type:'modify-might',amount:4,target:'self',duration:'turn'}; it resolved to trash with no unit changed (Gust Monk might unchanged)
findings.reason: Reproduced by loading the card via getCardRegistry(): ven-040-166 enriches to abilities=[{type:'spell',timing:'reaction',effect:{type:'modify-might',amount:4,target:'self',duration:'turn'}}], matching the observed chain item. Root cause is in the cards parser: packages/riftbound-cards/src/parser/impl/spells.ts:57-60 only strips simple "Choose a/an (friendly|enemy) unit[ here/there/at a battlefield]." preambles, so "Choose a friendly unit that's in combat with an enemy Fury unit or that's being chosen by an enemy Fury spell." is not recognized; parseEffects (impl/effects.ts:173-192) then sentence-splits, parseEffect returns undefined for the Choose sentence (dropped), and "Give it +4 [Might] this turn" is parsed by parseModifyMightEffect with pronoun "it" -> target 'self' (impl/effects-might.ts:243). With a string 'self' target the engine's play-time targeting (game-definition/moves/play/targeting.ts:104-105) treats it as a non-caster-chosen back-reference, so playSpell enumerates with no target/pendingChoice and the +4 resolves against the spell itself (no unit changed).

findings.what: +4 Might never applied through normal play flow
findings.expected: Chosen friendly unit gets +4 Might this turn
findings.observed: After untargeted (UI/enumerated) play + resolve, no unit's mightModifier changed. Only when targets were hand-injected via executeMove('playSpell',{...targets:[unitId]}) did meta.mightModifier=4 apply (UI showed 6) — a path the UI never offers
findings.reason: ven-040-166 (Decree of Focus) ships in ven.json with abilities:[null], so it is re-parsed from rulesText at load. The parser's sentence-split fallback in packages/riftbound-cards/src/parser/impl/effects.ts:174-190 silently drops the unparsable "Choose a friendly unit that's in combat with an enemy Fury unit or that's being chosen by an enemy Fury spell." sentence (parseEffect returns undefined; the spells.ts:57-60 Choose-preamble stripper also doesn't match the "that's in combat..." qualifier) and keeps only "Give it +4 [Might] this turn." -> {type:"modify-might", amount:4, duration:"turn", target:"self"} (verified by running getCardRegistry().get("ven-040-166") and parseEffects under bun). In the engine, play-spell.ts:330-336 computes isCardTarget=false because tgt is the bare string "self" (typeof tgt !== "string" fails), so no per-target playSpell variants are enumerated. On resolve, abilities/effects/_helpers.ts:35-48 getTargetIds falls to resolveTarget, and abilities/target-resolver.ts:97-98 maps "self" to ctx.sourceCardId — the spell card itself — so +4 mightModifier lands on the spell, never a unit. Only ctx.boundTargets (hand-injected targets, _helpers.ts:36-38) bypasses this, matching the observed behavior.

findings.what: Target restriction (in combat with enemy Fury unit) not enforced
findings.expected: Only a friendly unit in combat with an enemy Fury unit (or being chosen by an enemy Fury spell) is a legal choice; spell should not be playable with no legal target (rule 355.8)
findings.observed: playSpell was offered and resolved in main phase with no unit in combat at all; with explicit targets=[Mister Root] (combatRole null, at a different uncontested battlefield) the +4 was applied (might 1 -> 5 in UI)
findings.reason: ven-040-166 (Decree of Focus) has `abilities: [null]` in packages/riftbound-cards/src/data/sets/ven.json:1446, so it is re-parsed from rulesText. The parser drops the "Choose a friendly unit that's in combat with an enemy Fury unit or that's being chosen by an enemy Fury spell" clause entirely: the strip regex at packages/riftbound-cards/src/parser/impl/spells.ts:58 only handles "Choose a/an [friendly|enemy] unit[ at a battlefield|here|there]." and no parser anywhere encodes an "in combat with an enemy Fury unit" filter (grep for inCombatWith/in-combat-with in engine + parser: zero hits). Verified by running getCardRegistry(): the resulting ability is `{type:"spell", timing:"reaction", effect:{type:"modify-might", amount:4, target:"self", duration:"turn"}}` — a bare-string "self" target with no restriction. In the engine, packages/riftbound-engine/src/game-definition/moves/play/targeting.ts:262-264 returns `true` (always satisfiable) for bare-string targets, so the rule 355.8 no-legal-target gate never blocks play; and chain/resolve.ts:114 uses caller-supplied `resolved.targets` as boundTargets, so an explicit target like Mister Root receives the +4 regardless of combat state. Restriction is not enforced.

findings.what: No prompt to choose a friendly unit and a spell
findings.expected: Playing Riposte should require choosing a friendly unit and a spell on the chain (pendingChoice / target params); not playable when no spell is on the chain or no friendly unit exists (rule 355.8)
findings.observed: playSpell {cardId,playerId} offered with empty chain in main phase, and during beginning phase with only a triggered ability on chain and zero friendly units; when played with Progress Day on chain, no pendingChoice appeared; chain item effect is bare {type:'counter'}
findings.reason: Riposte's card def (riftbound-cards/src/cards/sfd/riposte.ts:4-16) has no hand-authored abilities; enrich-cards.ts parses rulesText, and running parseAbilities on it yields a bare `{type:"spell", effect:{type:"counter"}}` with no target descriptor (friendly-unit choice and buff dropped entirely). In play-spell.ts:172-179/297 the gate spellEffectHasLegalTargets (targeting.ts:238-251) returns true for an effect with no target/target1/target2, so the spell is offered with an empty chain and zero friendly units, and no per-target variants / pendingChoice are produced. No counter-specific chain gate exists in play-spell.ts. At resolution, abilities/effects/counter.ts:5-20 just marks the item below it on the chain countered (any item, including a triggered ability) with no choice and no might buff.

findings.what: Might buff equal to countered spell's Energy cost not applied
findings.expected: After countering Progress Day (cost 6), the chosen friendly unit (Treasure Hunter, might 1) gets +6 Might this turn
findings.observed: Progress Day was countered correctly, but Treasure Hunter meta has no mightModifier and UI might unchanged; same result when targets [unitId, spellCardId] were injected via executeMove. Parsed ability in sfd.json is a 'sequence' with effects:[] and runtime effect is only {type:'counter'}
findings.reason: riposte.ts declares no `abilities`, so enrich-cards.ts:29 runs parseAbilities on rulesText. Verified by running the parser: output is only {effect:{type:"counter"},timing:"reaction",type:"spell"}. Root cause: packages/riftbound-cards/src/parser/impl/effects-control.ts:29 — regex /^Counter (a spell.*|an? .+spell.*|that spell.*)\.?$/i greedily matches "Counter that spell and give that unit +Might equal to that spell's Energy cost this turn" and returns bare {type:"counter"} (line 33), discarding the "+Might equal to Energy cost" clause. Engine handle_counter (abilities/effects/counter.ts:5-21) only sets countered=true; no buff effect exists, so Treasure Hunter never gets a mightModifier.

findings.what: Chain overlay blocks playing reactions by click
findings.expected: While holding chain priority ('play a reaction spell or pass'), player can click the playable Riposte in hand or the sidebar 'Play Spell Riposte' action button
findings.observed: #chainOverlay (position fixed, inset 0, z-index 1500, pointer-events auto) covers hand and sidebar; document.elementFromPoint at both the hand card and the sidebar button returns chainOverlay; Playwright clicks on both time out; modal itself only renders Pass
findings.reason: css/gameplay.css:634-645: `.chain-overlay { position: fixed; inset: 0; background: rgba(5,3,15,0.7); z-index: 1500 }` with `.visible { display:flex }` and no pointer-events override — the only pointer-events:none rule is `.chain-overlay.targeting` (css:1731), and the `targeting` class is only ever toggled on the separate choice overlay (modals.js:32,41), never on #chainOverlay. renderChainOverlay (modals.js:208-218) adds `visible` to #chainOverlay whenever chain.active, and its action block (modals.js:288-303) emits only passChainPriority / resolveChain buttons — no reaction-spell moves. No hand or #actionsList rule has z-index >= 1500 (all >=1500 rules are zoom/drag/toast/other overlays). So while holding chain priority the full-viewport overlay intercepts clicks on the hand card and sidebar 'Play Spell' button, and the modal offers no alternative way to play the reaction.

findings.what: Wind Wall is playable with no spell on the chain (empty chain in main phase, or chain containing only a triggered ability)
findings.expected: Per rule 355.8 a spell must have valid choices for all targets to be put on the chain; 'Counter a spell' with no spell on the chain should not be offered/allowed
findings.observed: playSpell for Wind Wall was listed in moves with chain=null and with only the legend's start-of-turn ability on the chain; executing it consumed 3 energy + 2 calm and placed Wind Wall on the chain with effect {type:'counter'} and no target
findings.reason: Wind Wall's parsed spell ability is `{type:"counter"}` with no target descriptor (riftbound-cards/src/data/sets/ogn.json:2327-2329; parser/impl/effects-control.ts:33). play-spell.ts condition (line 172-179) and enumerator (line 297) gate only via spellEffectHasLegalTargets, which for an effect with no target/target1/target2/attacker/defender falls through targetDescriptorIsSatisfiable(undefined) -> true (targeting.ts:238-251, 259-261). Nothing checks that a spell exists on the chain; handle_counter (abilities/effects/counter.ts:8-19) just silently no-ops if the chain is empty. Repro via harness: P1 with 3 energy + 2 calm, Wind Wall in hand, empty chain -> can('cast')=true, cast ok, card on chain, energy 0, calm 0.

findings.what: Wind Wall countered a triggered ability
findings.expected: 'Counter a spell' can only target/counter a spell on the chain, never an ability
findings.observed: With only the legend (ogn-251-298) start-of-turn triggered ability on the chain, Wind Wall resolved and the ability chain item was marked countered:true
findings.reason: abilities/effects/counter.ts:14-17 — handle_counter unconditionally marks the top remaining chain item as countered (`targetItem.countered = true`) with no check on ChainItem.type (chain-state.ts:35 distinguishes "spell" | "permanent" | "ability"). Wind Wall's parsed effect is bare `{type:"counter"}` (ogn.json) with no spell-only target filter, and neither the handler nor the counterSpell move (moves/chain/counter.ts:37-44) restricts to type==="spell". So with only a triggered ability on the chain beneath Wind Wall, that ability item gets countered.

findings.what: No target prompt when multiple spells are on the chain
findings.expected: Player chooses which spell to counter (355.5/355.8 targeting choice made when played) — pendingChoice or per-target playSpell moves
findings.observed: With Mobilize (chain-2) and Premonition (chain-3) both on the chain, playSpell for Wind Wall had no targets param, no pendingChoice appeared, and on resolution the engine auto-countered the topmost spell (Premonition) without asking
findings.reason: riftbound-engine/src/abilities/effects/counter.ts:8-19 — handle_counter ignores any target: it takes `chain.items[items.length - 1]` (the new topmost item after the counter spell is popped) and sets countered=true. No effect.target is read, no pendingChoice is created, and the parser (riftbound-cards/src/parser/impl/effects-control.ts:26,33) emits `{ type: "counter" }` with no target descriptor, so playSpell has nothing to prompt on. With Mobilize and Premonition both on the chain, Wind Wall always counters the top one (Premonition) without a player choice, violating the targeting-at-play rule.

findings.what: Countered spell is not cleared from the chain immediately
findings.expected: Rule 425.1.a: a countered card 'does nothing and is cleared from the chain' and is placed in the trash as part of the counter resolving
findings.observed: After Wind Wall resolved, Premonition stayed on the chain flagged countered:true ('Premonition — spell (Countered)' in UI) and required another passChainPriority round before it went to trash (effect correctly did not fire: hand stayed 5, trash +1)
findings.reason: Counter effect only flags the target and leaves it on the chain. abilities/effects/counter.ts:14-17 (handle_counter) sets `targetItem.countered = true` in-place and does nothing else — no removal from chain.items, no zone move. Same in game-definition/moves/chain/counter.ts:56-57. The countered item is only popped later by resolveTopItem (chain/chain-state.ts:344-345) on the next all-pass, where executeResolvedItem skips it (resolve.ts:37-39) and settleResolvedSpellCard trashes it (resolve.ts:266-272). After Wind Wall pops, chain-state.ts:367-368 resets passes and hands priority to the countered item's controller, so another passChainPriority round is required. Rule 425.1.a/425.1.a.1 says a countered card is cleared from the chain and placed in trash as part of being countered — engine defers this.

findings.what: 'If your score is not within 3 points of the Victory Score, I enter ready' — the score condition is ignored; the unit always enters ready
findings.expected: Enter ready only when score <= VictoryScore-4 (e.g. 0-4 of 8); enter exhausted at 5-7
findings.observed: Parser emits static {effect:'enter-ready', condition:{type:'custom', text:...}} and play-unit.ts uses hasStaticEffect(cardId,'enter-ready') which never evaluates the condition. Empirical control in same game: Leona, Zealot (ogn-079-298, 'If an opponent's score IS within 3 points... I enter ready') entered READY with opponent at 0/8, while vanilla Shadow Fiend entered exhausted — proving the score condition on static enter-ready is not checked. Dragon entered ready at 0/8 (coincidentally correct) but would also enter ready at 5-7.
findings.reason: Parser emits for ven-091-166 a static ability {effect:{type:'enter-ready'}, condition:{type:'custom', text:'If your score is not within 3 points of the Victory Score'}} (verified by running parseAbilities on the rulesText; no hand-written override exists under riftbound-cards/src/cards/ — no ven/ dir). play-unit.ts:494-495 computes entersReady = replacedReady || hasStaticEffect(cardId,'enter-ready') || paidAccelerate, and hasStaticEffect (cost.ts:29-41) only matches ability.type==='static' && effect.type===effectType — it never reads or evaluates ability.condition. So the score condition is ignored and the unit always enters ready.

findings.what: 'When I attack, you may move any number of enemy units here each with 5 Might or less to their base' does nothing
findings.expected: After accepting the optional trigger, a prompt to choose any number of enemy units (<=5 Might) at that battlefield, and the chosen units move to player-2's base
findings.observed: Trigger fired on standardMove into battlefield with two enemy 1-Might Recruit tokens (chain item effect {type:'raw', text:'move any number of enemy units here each with 5 :rb_might: or less to their base.'}). After passChainPriority an opt-in pendingChoice 'Use Corrupted Dragon ability?' appeared; resolvePendingChoice accept:true cleared it with no unit-selection prompt and both Recruits remained at battlefield-player-2-bf-ogn-276-298; player-2 base empty. Effect is unparsed/unimplemented.
findings.reason: Parser (riftbound-cards/src/parser/index.ts parseAbilities) emits the attack trigger's effect as {type:"raw", text:"move any number of enemy units here each with 5 :rb_might: or less to their base."} — verified by running the parser on the card's rulesText. EFFECT_HANDLERS in riftbound-engine/src/abilities/effects/index.ts has no "raw" entry, so executeEffect (effect-executor.ts:145-151) falls to the `// default: no-op` branch. No card-specific override for ven-091-166/Corrupted Dragon exists anywhere in riftbound-cards/src or riftbound-engine/src. So after opt-in acceptance the effect resolves as a no-op: no target prompt, no move.

findings.expected: My Dazzling Aurora's end-of-turn trigger reveals/banishes Akshan and plays him ignoring cost; I may still pay the optional [body][body] additional cost (rule 356.1.b.3), his play trigger resolves and I take control of the enemy Dazzling Aurora. That stolen Aurora does NOT trigger this turn (Ending Step point already passed), but triggers at the end of my future turns; an Aurora taken before the Ending Step triggers normally that turn.
findings.observed: Exact card path is unreachable: when Aurora's reveal effect plays Akshan (chain item {type:move,to:choose} -> choose-destination base), the engine never offers the optional additional cost and no play-self trigger/take-control occurs even with 4 body power available -- Akshan just lands in base, enemy Aurora stays under player-2's control, and the turn immediately passes. The timing semantics themselves MATCH when simulated with sandbox transferControl: (a) control of an Aurora gained after endTurn (while the end-of-turn reveal trigger is on the chain) produced NO additional end-of-turn trigger that turn; (b) control gained during main phase (before Ending Step) made the taken Aurora trigger for its new controller at end of that turn (and the owner's copy, now enemy-controlled, did not trigger); (c) Akshan played from hand with paidAdditionalCost:true correctly steals the enemy Aurora, which then triggers at end of that turn and reveals from the controller's deck.
findings.notes: Bug is in the premise, not the timing: the reveal->'play it, ignoring its cost' path (abilities/effects/reveal.ts adds a bare move-to-choose chain item) bypasses the normal play pipeline, so optional additional costs (rule 356.1.b.3 explicitly allows paying them when cost is ignored) and Akshan's conditional 'When you play me' effect never get a chance. Trigger-runner controller-relative + evaluate-once-at-Ending-Step behavior agrees with the ruling. Opponent Aurora was created via sandbox duplicateCard into player-2 base; opponent priority passes driven via sandbox REST /move. Screenshot: /tmp/ruling-56312d623221a2f8.png

findings.expected: When playing Alpha Strike: friendly unit is chosen explicitly as a standard target; then up to N enemy units at battlefields are chosen as split targets where N = friendly unit's current Might (fewer, including zero, allowed; more than N not allowed). All targets locked at finalization; damage at resolution goes only to those locked targets.
findings.observed: Legal-move enumeration matches the ruling exactly: with Wizened Elder (Might 4) in base and 5 enemy units at a battlefield, playSpell moves were enumerated as [friendly, ...k enemies] for k=0..4 (C(5,k): 1/5/10/10/5) and never k=5; with Traveling Merchant (Might 2) as the friendly, k=0..2 only. Casting with [Elder, 3 enemies] put exactly those 4 ids in chain item targets; at resolution the split-damage pending choice offered only the 3 locked enemies, and 4 damage landed only on those 3 (1/1/2), untargeted enemies untouched -- all consistent with 355.14/355.15. HOWEVER, submitting executeMove('playSpell', targets=[Elder(Might 4) + all 5 enemies]) directly was ACCEPTED: energy was paid, the chain item locked in 6 targets (5 enemy split targets > Might 4), and it resolved dealing 1 damage to 4 of the 5 (after an odd 'choose-target remaining:1' prompt where the picked unit received 0). So the per-Might cap is enforced only by the move enumerator, not by move validation/finalization.
findings.notes: Core targeting model (explicit friendly target + split targets capped by Might, zero allowed, locked at finalization) is implemented correctly on the enumerated path; the divergence is a missing server-side validation of the split-target count against the friendly unit's Might when a raw move is submitted. Deflect-as-additional-cost portion not testable in goldfish (no Deflect enemy available). Side observations unrelated to this ruling: player-1 XP ticked 0->1 when the spell began resolving, before the split-damage choice was made (card file has a FIXME that kill-count is approximated via for-each 'damaged'); duplicateCard-created enemy units at damage==Might (2/2) were not removed, likely a dup-card artifact (their definitionId is the source instance id). Screenshots: /tmp/ruling-6b3effc73787ce91.png, /tmp/ruling-6b3effc73787ce91-chain.png.

findings.expected: With my only unit at a battlefield I control, Arcane Shift banishes it and the pending replay keeps the chain alive (closed state), so cleanup never makes the battlefield uncontrolled; the battlefield stays controlled throughout and I can choose to replay the unit there with no new contest/showdown.
findings.observed: Setup: P1 conquered Aspirant's Climb with a lone Legion Rearguard (controller=player-1), enemy dup unit at other BF. Cast Arcane Shift targets=[Rearguard, enemy]. On resolve: Rearguard -> banishment, enemy took 3 and died, Arcane Shift banished, and a triggered 'move to: choose' item (chain-3) was queued; BF still controller=player-1 at this point (good). But when chain-3 resolved into a pendingChoice (choose-destination, options [base, battlefield-player-1-bf-ogn-276-298]) the chain became null and cleanup ran: battlefields[player-1-bf-ogn-276-298].controller flipped to null BEFORE the unit was finalized. Picking the battlefield still succeeded (unit placed there), but because control had been dropped the arrival re-contested the BF (contested=true, contestedBy=player-1, showdownComplete=false, startShowdown/conquerBattlefield offered); after running that showdown the BF was left contested with controller=null. Net: replay-to-battlefield is allowed (matches the headline 'Yes'), but the engine loses control mid-resolution and triggers a spurious contest/showdown, contradicting the ruling's 'battlefield stays controlled'.
findings.notes: Root cause appears to be that the pending replay is modeled as a chain item that resolves into an off-chain pendingChoice; once the chain empties the open-state cleanup (323.6 step 4) fires while the unit is still in banishment. The destination list still offered the (now uncontrolled) battlefield, which is arguably a second inconsistency masking the first. Screenshot: /tmp/ruling-ee735b43996dcbd3.png. Side note: standardMove with destination 'battlefield-<bfId>' (instead of '<bfId>') silently removed the unit from all zones in an earlier attempt.
